contract.frozen: The text of a published definition never changes.
contract.versioning: A breaking change is a new id ending .v2, never an edit to .v1.
contract.retention: A superseded version stays served for at least 90 days.
contract.does_not_assert: Every definition states what it does NOT claim, because most misuse of a metric is reading in something it never said.

definitions.title: Distinct ACP clients
definitions.definition: Distinct addresses recorded as the client on an indexed ACP job.
definitions.method: Taken from the indexed client topic of JobCreated, JobFunded and Refunded.
excludes: Clients on jobs outside the scanned range.
does_not_assert: Demand size. A client can open many jobs, and many jobs pay nothing.

definitions.title: ACP jobs marked completed
definitions.definition: Jobs that received a JobCompleted event, which the contract emits with the evaluator that signed it off.
definitions.method: Latched true on first occurrence; a job cannot un-complete.
excludes: Jobs rejected, expired or still open.
does_not_assert: That the provider was paid. Completion and payment are separate events, and they do not always both happen.

definitions.title: Our ERC-8004 bound wallets seen in ACP events
definitions.definition: Distinct wallets bound to an ERC-8004 actor in our graph whose address appears in an indexed ACP Core event.
definitions.method: Join our open bindings against the ACP participant index.
excludes: Wallets we have not bound, and activity outside the indexed block range.
does_not_assert: That the agent sold or bought a job. We cannot decode what the events mean without a verified ABI.
Overlap between the ERC-8004 and Virtuals populations. They are counted separately and are mostly different sets.

definitions.title: ERC-8004 actors paid for ACP work
definitions.definition: Distinct actors in our graph whose bound wallet appears as the provider on an ACP job that released value above zero.
definitions.method: Join our open bindings against the decoded job table.
excludes: Actors we have not bound, and jobs outside the scanned range.
does_not_assert: Overlap between the ERC-8004 and Virtuals populations. They are counted separately and are largely different sets.

definitions.title: ACP Core events indexed
definitions.definition: Count of events emitted by the ACP Core contract within the block range we have scanned.
definitions.method: Summed as the cursor walks forward. A window that errors is skipped rather than retried forever, so the cursor cannot stall behind a plausible-looking number.
excludes: Skipped windows, and everything outside the indexed range.
does_not_assert: Job volume. Several events can belong to one job, and we cannot yet tell which.

definitions.title: ACP jobs funded into escrow
definitions.definition: Jobs that received a JobFunded event carrying an amount above zero.
definitions.method: Amount read from the event's data word as USDC at six decimals, a unit confirmed by matching a funding event against the USDC transfer in its own transaction receipt.
excludes: Jobs funded with zero, which are counted as jobs but not as funded.
does_not_assert: That the work happened. Escrow is money set aside, not money earned.

definitions.title: USDC funded into ACP escrow
definitions.definition: Total value placed into escrow through JobFunded events within the scanned range.
definitions.method: Summed per job, because a job can be funded more than once.
excludes: Zero-value funding events.
does_not_assert: Revenue. Escrowed money can be refunded, and refunds are tracked separately.

definitions.title: ACP jobs indexed
definitions.definition: Distinct Agent Commerce Protocol job ids seen in events from the ACP Core contract on Base within the scanned block range.
definitions.method: Decoded from the verified implementation ABI. Every observed topic resolves to a named event; none is named by guesswork.
excludes: Blocks outside the scanned range. The index walks forward from thirty days before its first run.
does_not_assert: That a job was worked, delivered or paid. A job id exists from the moment one is created, and most never pay anything.
Job volume for Virtuals as a whole. It is what this contract emitted in the range we read.

definitions.title: ACP jobs that actually paid a provider
definitions.definition: Jobs whose summed PaymentReleased value is greater than zero.
definitions.method: Value, not event count. A PaymentReleased carrying zero is not a payment, and most of them carry zero.
excludes: Jobs with a payout event that released nothing.
Evaluator fees, counted separately.
does_not_assert: A count of payout events. The gap between the two is published as the zero-value payout rate, because counting events instead of value would overstate this economy several times over.

definitions.title: ACP providers that were actually paid
definitions.definition: Distinct provider addresses on jobs whose released value exceeded zero.
definitions.method: Value-gated, exactly as the paid-jobs count is.
excludes: Providers whose only payouts released zero.
does_not_assert: That they are agents. The contract records an address.

definitions.title: USDC released to ACP providers
definitions.definition: Total value released to providers through PaymentReleased events within the scanned range.
definitions.method: USDC at six decimals on Base, confirmed against a transaction receipt rather than inferred from the magnitude of the numbers.
excludes: Zero-value releases, which add nothing by construction.
Evaluator fees and refunds, both tracked separately.
does_not_assert: The size of the agent economy. It is one job protocol on one chain over one window, and the tickets are cents.
That the recipient is an agent rather than a person operating one. The contract records an address, not an identity.

definitions.title: Addresses seen in ACP Core events
definitions.definition: Distinct addresses appearing in an indexed topic of an event emitted by the Virtuals ACP Core contract on Base.
definitions.method: eth_getLogs over the contract on the keyless public mesh, 1,900 blocks per request. An address is taken from a topic only when its leading twelve bytes are zero — job ids and hashes share those slots and are not addresses.
excludes: Blocks outside the indexed range. The index starts seven days before its first run and walks forward; `blocks_behind` is published beside it.
does_not_assert: A job, a settlement, or a payment. We hold no verified ABI for the implementation contract, so request, negotiation, settlement, cancellation and evaluation are indistinguishable to us today.
L7. Participation in an event is evidence of being on the job rail in practice rather than only in a catalog field, and it is not evidence that anyone paid anyone.

definitions.title: Distinct ACP providers
definitions.definition: Distinct addresses recorded as the provider on an indexed ACP job.
definitions.method: Taken from the indexed provider topic of JobCreated, ProviderSet, JobSubmitted and PaymentReleased.
excludes: Providers on jobs outside the scanned range.
does_not_assert: That each address is a separate operator. One operator can run many providers.

definitions.title: Virtuals agent wallets observed in ACP events
definitions.definition: Distinct sole-declarant Virtuals agent wallets whose address appears in an indexed ACP Core event.
definitions.method: Join our bound Virtuals wallets against the participant index. Wallets shared by several identities are excluded, as everywhere else.
excludes: Shared operator wallets.
Agents whose ACP activity falls outside the indexed block range.
does_not_assert: That the agent sold or bought a job. It asserts its wallet was a party to an ACP Core event.
A rate over the catalog. Read it against the indexed range and the bound set, both published beside it.

definitions.title: Virtuals agent wallets paid for ACP work
definitions.definition: Distinct sole-declarant Virtuals agent wallets that appear as the provider on an ACP job which released value above zero.
definitions.method: Join our bound Virtuals wallets against the decoded job table. Wallets shared by several identities are excluded, as everywhere else on this site.
excludes: Shared operator wallets.
Jobs outside the scanned range.
Zero-value payouts.
does_not_assert: That every paying Virtuals agent is here. Only wallets we have bound, on jobs we have indexed, are counted \u2014 this is a floor.
A rate over the catalog. Read it against the bound set and the indexed range.

definitions.title: USDC paid to Virtuals agent wallets for ACP work
definitions.definition: Value released to providers whose address is a bound Virtuals agent wallet.
definitions.method: Summed from the same decoded job table, value-gated.
excludes: Zero-value releases, shared wallets, and jobs outside the range.
does_not_assert: Agent revenue in general. It is the slice of one job protocol that lands on wallets we have bound.

definitions.title: Share of paid-out ACP jobs that released nothing
definitions.definition: One minus the share of jobs with a payout event whose released value was above zero.
definitions.method: Both counts come from one query so they cannot be read from different instants.
excludes: Jobs that never reached a payout event at all.
does_not_assert: Fraud or failure. A zero-value release is a legitimate outcome for a free or cancelled job.
That the remaining payments are large. They are cents.

definitions.title: Bankr fee recipients bound to a tracked agent
definitions.definition: Base fee recipients from the registry that are also wallets currently bound to an identity in this graph.
definitions.method: Join against live bindings. This is the overlap between the token-launch population and the registered-agent population, and it is the denominator that makes the paying figures readable.
excludes: Closed bindings.
Chains other than Base.
does_not_assert: That the populations should overlap. A zero is a finding about how separate the two economies are, not a defect.
That a bound recipient is an agent doing work. Binding is identity, not activity.

definitions.title: Bankr creator fee share, cited
definitions.definition: The creator's portion of lifetime fees across indexed launches, as computed and published by Bankr's own fee endpoint.
definitions.method: Their number. Summed from their endpoint, not reproduced by us.
excludes: Launches with no fee record.
does_not_assert: That the creator claimed it. The endpoint reports both claimable and claimed, and this is the earned figure.

definitions.title: Distinct Bankr deployers
definitions.definition: Distinct deployer addresses across the indexed launches, as published in the operator's registry rows.
definitions.method: Read from the registry's deployerAddress field.
excludes: Rows with no deployer published.
does_not_assert: That a deployer is an agent, or that it is distinct from the fee recipient.

definitions.title: Share of Bankr launches with any fee record
definitions.definition: Indexed launches with a fee record above zero, divided by the launches we have actually asked the fee endpoint about.
definitions.method: The denominator is ASKED, never indexed. Dividing by the indexed count would fold “we have not got round to asking” into “earned nothing”, which are different facts and only one of them is about Bankr.
excludes: Launches not yet asked about.
does_not_assert: A complete count. Bankr's batch endpoint sometimes omits a token that its own per-token endpoint shows did earn fees, on both chains and at any launch age, so the share is an under-count; how often is re-measured on every run.

A stable property of Bankr launches. The share varies several-fold by launch week and by chain, so it describes the indexed window only. Nor is it a floor: an earlier version of this definition said so, on the theory that a newest-first walk skews young, and the data disproved it - older launch weeks earn fees less often. Withdrawn 2026-09-14.
That the fee-earning launches are typical. Fees are extremely concentrated — a single token can be a third of the total — so no average here describes a real launch.

definitions.title: Bankr launches indexed
definitions.definition: Distinct token addresses read from Bankr's own public launch registry.
definitions.method: We page their canonical discover feed, which they pointed us to publicly, and store the row. Membership is read from the operator's registry, never inferred from a hook, a beneficiary or a token-address suffix.
excludes: Launches the registry has not published.
Pages beyond the walk's current cursor position, which is published beside the count.
does_not_assert: That a launch is an agent. A token launch is a token launch, and none of these rows enters this site's actor count.
A complete census of Bankr launches. It is what their feed had returned to us by the timestamp beside it.

definitions.title: Bankr fee recipients observed paying
definitions.definition: Base fee recipients from the registry that our own payment scan has observed making a payment, after pass-through routing hops and pre-registration history are removed.
definitions.method: Join the registry's fee recipients against our verified payment set. This is the half of the fee-to-compute loop that only we can check.
excludes: Pass-through hops.
Payments before the payer's identity existed.
Chains other than Base.
does_not_assert: THAT A ZERO MEANS THEY NEVER PAY. Our payment scan follows wallets bound to identities in this graph and nothing else, so a fee recipient outside that set cannot appear here whatever it does with its money. The width of the scan is published beside this number for exactly that reason.
That an observed payment bought compute. That is the separate named-seller metric.

definitions.title: Bankr platform fee share, cited
definitions.definition: The platform's portion of lifetime fees across indexed launches, as computed and published by Bankr's own fee endpoint.
definitions.method: Their number. Summed from their endpoint, not reproduced by us.
excludes: Launches with no fee record.
does_not_assert: Bankr's revenue. It is the platform share on the launches we have indexed and asked about, which is a subset of theirs.

definitions.title: Distinct Bankr fee recipients
definitions.definition: Distinct fee recipient addresses across the indexed launches, as published in the operator's own registry rows.
definitions.method: Read from the registry's feeRecipientAddress field, which was populated on every row we have seen.
excludes: Rows with no fee recipient published.
does_not_assert: That the address collected anything. It is the address named to collect.
That one address is one person. A single operator can hold many, and many launches can share one.

definitions.title: Bankr fee recipient payments to a named seller
definitions.definition: Payments from a registry fee recipient to an address in our named-seller set. This is the metric that decides whether the fee-to-compute loop closes.
definitions.method: Verified payments only, joined to the x402 recipient set. The loop is reported as closing if and only if this is above zero.
excludes: Pass-through hops.
Payments to addresses we cannot name as sellers.
does_not_assert: That a zero disproves the loop. It means unmeasured. See the scan-scope figure published with it.
The value of compute bought. It counts payments, not dollars.

definitions.title: Bankr launch fees, cited
definitions.definition: Sum of lifetime total fees across indexed launches, as computed and published by Bankr's own fee endpoint.
definitions.method: THIS IS THEIR NUMBER, NOT OURS. We batch their endpoint and add up what it returns. We did not reproduce the fee accounting from chain data and we do not present this as a measurement of ours — the _cited suffix in the metric name is there so the label survives being quoted out of context.
excludes: Launches the endpoint has no record for.
Launches not yet asked about.
does_not_assert: Our own verification. An independently measured figure would be named without _cited, and this one is not.
That fees were withdrawn, spent, or converted into anything. Accrual is not a payment.
That the USD total only rises. It is Bankr's USD valuation, which moves with prices, so it can dip slightly when ETH falls even though fees earned in token units only rise.
A complete total. Bankr's batch endpoint sometimes omits tokens that did earn fees, so the total is an under-count.
Anything about this site's own spending headline, which excludes every number on this page.

definitions.title: Bankr launches with any fee record
definitions.definition: Indexed launches for which the operator's fee endpoint returns a record with total fees above zero.
definitions.method: Batched against their public token-fee-summary endpoint. A token the endpoint has nothing for is simply omitted from the response, and we record that omission rather than treating it as zero-by-assumption.
excludes: Launches not yet asked about — the asked count is published beside this one.
does_not_assert: That the remaining launches earned nothing. It asserts the operator's endpoint has no fee record for them.
A rate over all launches unless you divide by the asked count, not the indexed count.

definitions.title: USD value of observed agent payments into CCTP
definitions.definition: The summed USD value of those same payments.
definitions.method: As above, summing the recorded USD value.
excludes: The same exclusions as the event count.
does_not_assert: That a zero means agents hold no cross-chain balances. We observe outbound payments on Base, not balances elsewhere.

definitions.title: Observed agent payments into Circle CCTP
definitions.definition: Payments from a bound agent wallet whose recipient is a Circle CCTP TokenMessenger or MessageTransmitter — a USDC burn destined for another chain.
definitions.method: Match the recipient of every observed payment against Circle's own published CCTP contract addresses. Both CCTP V2 and the older V1 TokenMessenger are watched, so a zero cannot be an artefact of tracking only the new contract.
excludes: Cross-chain movement through bridge aggregators rather than CCTP directly. That is a different measurement and we have not made it yet.
Chains other than Base, because that is where our payment scan runs.
does_not_assert: That agents do not move between chains. It says only that they do not use Circle's own bridge to do it — a bridge aggregator sits among our busiest counterparties.
That CCTP is unused generally. This counts our tracked agents, not the protocol.

definitions.title: CCTP contract addresses watched
definitions.definition: How many Circle CCTP contract addresses the exit check is matching against.
definitions.method: Counted from the static map built from Circle's published contract reference. Published so that a zero exit count can be read next to the size of the net that caught nothing.
excludes: CCTP deployments on chains our payment scan does not cover.
does_not_assert: That this is every CCTP contract Circle operates.

definitions.title: Registrations in the graph
definitions.definition: Every ERC-8004 registration on Base that has an actor in our graph, with its owner wallet bound by ownerOf. Since 27 September 2026 that is every registration with a non-burn owner, read daily from the registry's owner list; before, only registrations the prober had sampled.
definitions.method: Alchemy NFT API getOwnersForContract over the Identity registry, then the same actor and binding rows the prober writes, at liveness 0.
excludes: Registrations whose owner is a burn or zero address.
does_not_assert: Anything above L0 for a registration the prober has not graded and the payment scan has not read.

definitions.title: Bound wallets
definitions.definition: Distinct wallets with an open binding to a registration: its owner (ownerOf), its declared agent wallet, or a wallet proven by signature.
definitions.method: Distinct wallet over bindings with no valid_to.
excludes: Closed bindings (kept as an audit trail).
does_not_assert: Who operates the wallet. One wallet can own many registrations, and an owner key is evidence of control, not identity.

definitions.title: ERC-8004 registrations across the chains we read
definitions.definition: Registrations with a current holder in the ERC-8004 Identity registry on Base, plus those on Ethereum, Arbitrum One, OP Mainnet and Polygon PoS, each read by us from the registry's own owner list.
definitions.method: census.registrations.owned.v1 plus xchain.registrations.v1, both from Alchemy's NFT API on each chain, daily.
excludes: Chains we do not read (BNB Smart Chain issuance is watched separately and is large).
Burn and zero holders.
does_not_assert: Agreement with third-party counters such as 8004scan or agenteconomy.to, which index more chains and registries; they are published beside this figure as context, not added to it.
definitions.source: AFG-Pulse registry census and other-chain census

definitions.title: Registrations with a current owner
definitions.definition: ERC-8004 Identity registrations on Base returned with a current holder by the registry's owner list.
definitions.method: Alchemy NFT API getOwnersForContract over the Identity registry (0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432), daily.
does_not_assert: That a registration is an operating agent. It is a name that exists.

definitions.title: Bound wallets not yet scanned for payments
definitions.definition: Wallets with an open binding whose outbound stablecoin transfers we have never read. While this is above zero the L7 count is a floor.
definitions.method: wallets.last_pay_check IS NULL over open bindings. The sweep reads every such wallet's stablecoin Transfer logs over the whole registry era, 2,000 wallets per query: a wallet that sent nothing is marked checked, a wallet that sent something goes to the per-wallet scan.
does_not_assert: That an unscanned wallet has paid anyone.

definitions.title: WETH/USDC routed price
definitions.definition: The USDC a routed swap of one WETH would return, quoted by the 0x aggregator.
definitions.method: A live quote, not an oracle read. It is an executable price including routing, which is why it can differ from a spot index.
excludes: Gas and slippage beyond what the quote itself accounts for.
does_not_assert: That any trade happened at this price. It is a quote, and quotes expire.

definitions.title: WETH/USDC price, Uniswap v3 pool on Base (on-chain)
definitions.definition: The mid price implied by slot0 of the Uniswap v3 WETH/USDC 0.05% pool on Base (0xd0b53d92…f224): sqrtPriceX96 squared, scaled by the tokens' decimals. The venue's own state, read on the public mesh every five minutes.
definitions.method: eth_call slot0() on the pool; token0 WETH, token1 USDC (verified 27 Sep 2026). No vendor, no key. Replaces convert.weth.0x.v1, whose vendor paused quote-only use on 27 Sep 2026.
excludes: Fees and slippage: a mid price, not an executable quote for a given size.
does_not_assert: Any connection to agents. Pure market context.
definitions.source: Uniswap v3 pool on Base, on-chain

definitions.title: Observed agent payments that leave the chain
definitions.definition: Payments landing on any labelled bridge, whether Circle's own CCTP contracts or a third-party aggregator.
definitions.method: The union of the bridge-category labels. Published because the CCTP check alone reads zero and would leave the false impression that agents never move between chains — they do, just not through Circle.
excludes: Bridges we have not labelled.
does_not_assert: That the money arrived. A burn or a lock on Base is not proof of a mint elsewhere.

definitions.title: Observed agent payments to agents moving money off the chain (count)
definitions.definition: Payments landing on a cross-chain bridge or bridge aggregator.
definitions.method: Match the recipient of every observed payment against a label config in which each entry carries a citable basis — a verified contract name or a curated explorer name tag — and a link a reader can open.
excludes: Every destination we cannot name from a citable source, which is most addresses by count. Read this beside counterparty_labelled_share rather than as a share of all agent spending.
does_not_assert: Which chain the money arrived on. We observe the exit from Base, not the destination — that needs the aggregator's own message decoded, which we have not done.
Who operates the contract. A label describes what the code does; naming a company is a separate claim needing separate evidence, and we do not make it.

definitions.title: Observed agent payments to agents moving money off the chain (value)
definitions.definition: Payments landing on a cross-chain bridge or bridge aggregator.
definitions.method: Match the recipient of every observed payment against a label config in which each entry carries a citable basis — a verified contract name or a curated explorer name tag — and a link a reader can open.
excludes: Every destination we cannot name from a citable source, which is most addresses by count. Read this beside counterparty_labelled_share rather than as a share of all agent spending.
does_not_assert: Which chain the money arrived on. We observe the exit from Base, not the destination — that needs the aggregator's own message decoded, which we have not done.
Who operates the contract. A label describes what the code does; naming a company is a separate claim needing separate evidence, and we do not make it.

definitions.title: Observed agent payments to agents supplying or repaying on a lending protocol (count)
definitions.definition: Payments landing on a lending-protocol adapter or market.
definitions.method: Match the recipient of every observed payment against a label config in which each entry carries a citable basis — a verified contract name or a curated explorer name tag — and a link a reader can open.
excludes: Every destination we cannot name from a citable source, which is most addresses by count. Read this beside counterparty_labelled_share rather than as a share of all agent spending.
does_not_assert: That the agent is borrowing rather than supplying. The direction is not resolved from the transfer alone.
Who operates the contract. A label describes what the code does; naming a company is a separate claim needing separate evidence, and we do not make it.

definitions.title: Observed agent payments to agents supplying or repaying on a lending protocol (value)
definitions.definition: Payments landing on a lending-protocol adapter or market.
definitions.method: Match the recipient of every observed payment against a label config in which each entry carries a citable basis — a verified contract name or a curated explorer name tag — and a link a reader can open.
excludes: Every destination we cannot name from a citable source, which is most addresses by count. Read this beside counterparty_labelled_share rather than as a share of all agent spending.
does_not_assert: That the agent is borrowing rather than supplying. The direction is not resolved from the transfer alone.
Who operates the contract. A label describes what the code does; naming a company is a separate claim needing separate evidence, and we do not make it.

definitions.title: Observed agent payments into DEX pools and swap routers (count)
definitions.definition: Payments whose recipient is a labelled DEX pool or swap router: the stablecoin was exchanged for another token in the same transaction. Buying an asset, not a service.
definitions.method: Match the recipient against the label config (verified pool contract names such as UniswapV3Pool and CLPool; for unverified routers, sampled receipts showing the stablecoin swapped in the same transaction).
excludes: Swaps routed through contracts we have not labelled.
Swaps that begin from a non-stablecoin, which are never recorded as payments.
does_not_assert: What was bought or why. A swap into WETH to pay gas and a swap into a memecoin look the same here.

definitions.title: Observed agent payments into DEX pools and swap routers (value)
definitions.definition: USD value of the payments in cp.cat.swap.events.v1.
definitions.method: As cp.cat.swap.events.v1.
excludes: As cp.cat.swap.events.v1.
does_not_assert: That the agent kept what it bought.

definitions.title: Observed agent payments to agents paying for work held in escrow (count)
definitions.definition: Payments landing on an escrow contract whose own verified source declares an order lifecycle — created, funded, accepted, delivered, settled — with a dispute layer above it.
definitions.method: Match the recipient of every observed payment against a label config in which each entry carries a citable basis — a verified contract name or a curated explorer name tag — and a link a reader can open.
excludes: Every destination we cannot name from a citable source, which is most addresses by count. Read this beside counterparty_labelled_share rather than as a share of all agent spending.
does_not_assert: That the work was done, or done well. We observe money entering escrow, not a delivery being accepted.
Who operates the contract. A label describes what the code does; naming a company is a separate claim needing separate evidence, and we do not make it.

definitions.title: Observed agent payments to agents paying for work held in escrow (value)
definitions.definition: Payments landing on an escrow contract whose own verified source declares an order lifecycle — created, funded, accepted, delivered, settled — with a dispute layer above it.
definitions.method: Match the recipient of every observed payment against a label config in which each entry carries a citable basis — a verified contract name or a curated explorer name tag — and a link a reader can open.

definitions.title: Observed agent payments to agents parking cash in a vault (count)
definitions.definition: Payments landing on an ERC-4626 or similar vault contract.
definitions.method: Match the recipient of every observed payment against a label config in which each entry carries a citable basis — a verified contract name or a curated explorer name tag — and a link a reader can open.
excludes: Every destination we cannot name from a citable source, which is most addresses by count. Read this beside counterparty_labelled_share rather than as a share of all agent spending.
does_not_assert: That the deposit earned anything. It records where cash went, not what it returned.
Who operates the contract. A label describes what the code does; naming a company is a separate claim needing separate evidence, and we do not make it.

definitions.title: Observed agent payments to agents parking cash in a vault (value)
definitions.definition: Payments landing on an ERC-4626 or similar vault contract.
definitions.method: Match the recipient of every observed payment against a label config in which each entry carries a citable basis — a verified contract name or a curated explorer name tag — and a link a reader can open.

Who operates the contract. A label describes what the code does; naming a company is a separate claim needing separate evidence, and we do not make it.

definitions.title: Share of counterparties that are contracts
definitions.definition: Of the counterparty addresses we have classified, the share whose on-chain code is non-empty and is not an EIP-7702 delegation designator.
definitions.method: One eth_getCode per address, re-checked monthly. A designator (0xef0100 + 20 bytes) is classified as a delegated EOA rather than a contract, because it is a wallet running someone else's code.
excludes: Addresses we have not yet classified — they are excluded from the denominator, never assumed.
does_not_assert: Anything about what the contracts do.

definitions.title: Distinct addresses our agents have paid
definitions.definition: Every distinct destination address across observed agent payments.
definitions.method: Counted from observed payments after the pre-registration exclusion. The full set is published.
excludes: Destinations of excluded payments.
does_not_assert: That these are sellers. Most are contracts, and we do not claim to know what a given contract does unless we can name it from a citable source.

definitions.title: Counterparty addresses carrying a label
definitions.definition: How many destination addresses have a label with a citable basis.
definitions.method: Counted from the label config.
does_not_assert: That labelling is complete. It is deliberately small: an address enters only with evidence a reader can open.

definitions.title: Observed agent payments with a named destination
definitions.definition: The raw count behind counterparty_labelled_share: payments whose recipient carries a label with a citable basis.
definitions.method: Counted in the same pass as the category metrics, so the categories always sum to exactly this number.
excludes: Pre-registration and pass-through payments, like every payment total.
does_not_assert: That a labelled destination is understood. We know what the contract calls itself, not what any payment was for.

definitions.title: Share of observed agent payments with a named destination
definitions.definition: Payments whose recipient we can name from a citable source, divided by all observed payments.
definitions.method: Counted from the label config. This is the honesty gauge for every category share above it: a category share means little without knowing how much of the map is still blank.
does_not_assert: That the unlabelled remainder is unimportant. By value it is the majority, because the single largest actor pays destinations we have not named.
That a labelled destination is understood. We know what the contract calls itself, not what any given payment was for.

definitions.title: Destinations paid by three or more different agents
definitions.definition: Counterparties that have received payments from at least three distinct tracked agents.
definitions.method: Group observed payments by destination and count distinct payers. Ranked by distinct payers rather than volume, because volume is dominated by one large actor while the number of separate agents choosing a destination cannot be faked by a whale.
excludes: Destinations below the threshold.
does_not_assert: That these are the best or busiest services. Three payers is a low bar, chosen because the population above it is still small.

definitions.title: Share of paying agents sharing one destination
definitions.definition: The number of distinct agents that have paid the single most popular counterparty, divided by the number of distinct agents we have observed paying anyone.
definitions.method: Counterparties ranked by DISTINCT paying actors, not by volume. Volume is dominated by one large actor — roughly two thirds of all value comes from a single registration — so ranking by it would measure that actor rather than the market. Distinct payers cannot be inflated by one whale.
excludes: Payments excluded as pre-registration.
Self-transfers.
does_not_assert: That the destination is a seller, a service, or an operator. It is an address that many agents pay. Most top destinations are CONTRACTS, and we do not read intent from bytecode.
That the agents are unrelated to each other. A single operator running many registrations would look like many payers here, and we cannot currently tell the difference.

definitions.title: Counterparties classified by code
definitions.definition: Addresses among the largest recipients of counted agent spending whose code we have read: contract, plain key, or key delegated to code under EIP-7702.
definitions.method: eth_getCode, 40 addresses per batch, through the governor.
does_not_assert: What the contract does or who runs it.

definitions.title: Share of agent money paid to contracts
definitions.window: all time, over the top 500 counterparties by counted USD
definitions.definition: Of the counted agent spending that went to the 500 addresses receiving the most of it, the share that went to addresses holding contract code (not a plain key, not a key delegated to code under EIP-7702).
definitions.method: eth_getCode on each address, re-read monthly. A 23-byte 0xef0100 designator is a delegated key, counted as a wallet, not a contract.
excludes: Counterparties outside the top 500.
does_not_assert: What the contract is. Naming comes from the counterparty labels, which are curated with a source each.

definitions.title: Detections logged
definitions.definition: Every anomaly our detectors have recorded: mint bursts, retry storms, endpoints that never answer, identities that changed owner, delegations outside the allowlist.
definitions.method: Queries over our own measurements, hourly, no external calls. Each detection is a row with a time and an evidence object. History before 2026-09-11 is carried over from open_incidents, which counted exactly these rows under a name that promised something else.
excludes: States. A low liveness score is a measurement, not a detection, and never appears here.
does_not_assert: That a detection is wrongdoing. Most of the log is mint bursts, and bulk minting is legitimate behaviour that changes what a registration count means rather than evidence of abuse.
That the log is exhaustive. It holds what these detectors can see in what we have measured.

definitions.title: Detections in the last 7 days
definitions.definition: Detections whose event time falls inside the last seven days.
definitions.method: Counted from the same log. Dated by when the event happened, not by when we noticed it, so a backfill does not make last week look busy.
excludes: Older detections, which remain in the log.
does_not_assert: That activity is rising or falling. One week is a count, not a trend.

definitions.title: Distinct Doppler integrator addresses recovered
definitions.definition: Distinct integrator addresses read out of launch calldata.
definitions.method: The integrator is field 11 of Airlock's CreateParams, so it is readable when create() is the top-level call. Through an ERC-4337 UserOperation it is buried in an inner call and the launch is recorded as unattributed.
excludes: Every launch routed through account abstraction, which is the majority. This count is therefore a floor and is not a measure of how many front-ends use Doppler.
does_not_assert: That any integrator address belongs to a named product. Doppler's documentation names Zora, Paragraph, Noice and Bankr as integrators, but the on-chain addresses are not published anywhere we can cite, so we do not attach names to them.
That integrator share can be measured from this. It cannot, while most launches bury the field.

definitions.title: Doppler token launches in the last 30 days
definitions.definition: Airlock Create events with a block timestamp inside the last 30 days.
definitions.method: Counted from the indexed launch table. Published ONLY once the sweep has reached the chain head — mid-backfill this counts how far we have read rather than what happened, so it is withheld instead.
excludes: Everything outside the window, and everything in blocks not yet swept.
does_not_assert: That launch volume is demand. A launch is a contract deployment; most of these tokens will never trade meaningfully.

definitions.title: Doppler token launches indexed
definitions.definition: Distinct tokens created through the Doppler Airlock launch controller, counted from its Create event.
definitions.method: Sweep Airlock logs on the keyless Base RPC mesh in 9,999-block windows. The watermark never advances past a window that failed to read, so a gap is a stall rather than silent data loss.
excludes: Tokens launched by any other mechanism. This is one launch layer, not the whole of Base.
does_not_assert: That these are agent tokens. Doppler is general-purpose infrastructure; its documentation names Zora, Paragraph, Noice and Bankr among its integrators, and most launches will be neither agents nor businesses.

definitions.title: Share of Doppler launches with no external fee beneficiary
definitions.definition: Launches whose fee-beneficiary split names nobody except Doppler's own protocol address, divided by all launches carrying a split.
definitions.method: Decode the (address, share) array emitted by the DopplerHookInitializer at launch. The protocol beneficiary is identified by appearing on essentially every launch rather than by hardcoding an address, so a redeployment does not silently break the measure.
excludes: Launches that emitted no split event — different migrator paths do not emit one.
does_not_assert: That such a launch earns nothing. It means no creator address was named in the split, not that the creator has no other claim.

definitions.title: Share of Doppler fee recipients that appear exactly once
definitions.definition: External fee-recipient addresses named in exactly one launch split, divided by all external fee recipients.
definitions.method: Group the beneficiary table by address, excluding Doppler's own protocol beneficiary, and count those with a single launch.
excludes: Doppler's protocol beneficiary, which is present on every launch by construction.
does_not_assert: That a one-launch recipient is inactive or abandoned. It has launched once so far, which is the ordinary case.

definitions.title: Distinct Doppler launch fee recipients
definitions.definition: Distinct addresses named as fee beneficiaries in a launch split, excluding Doppler's own protocol beneficiary.
definitions.method: Decode the (address, share) array emitted at launch and count distinct addresses. The protocol beneficiary is identified by appearing on essentially every launch rather than by hardcoding it, so a redeployment does not silently corrupt the count.
excludes: Doppler's protocol beneficiary, present on every launch by construction.
Launches whose migrator path emits no split event.
does_not_assert: That a recipient is an agent, a company, or a person. It is an address that stands to receive fees.
That the recipient controls the token or the launch. It is the address the split names.

definitions.title: Recent Doppler launches whose signing route is classified
definitions.definition: Launches in the last 30 days for which we have fetched the transaction and recorded how it was signed.
definitions.method: One transaction fetch per launch, filled in progressively newest-first rather than all at once.
excludes: Launches not yet classified.
does_not_assert: That the classified set is a random sample. It is biased toward recent launches by construction, which is why it is only ever used as the denominator for a same-window rate.

definitions.title: Share of Doppler token launches signed by a smart account
definitions.definition: Of the Airlock launches in the last 30 days whose signing route we have classified, the share whose transaction was sent to an ERC-4337 EntryPoint or the Doppler Bundler rather than being a direct call from an externally owned account.
definitions.method: Read the top-level `to` of each launch transaction. EntryPoint v0.6 and v0.7 both count as account abstraction; counting only v0.7 understates the share by about nine points.
excludes: Launches whose route we have not classified yet. Classification costs one transaction fetch each and is filled in progressively; the denominator is always the number actually classified, published beside it as doppler_launches_route_classified_30d.
does_not_assert: That a smart-account launch was made by an autonomous agent. A smart account is a contract wallet, and a person can sign through one; this measures the wallet type, not who decided.
Anything about which front-end drove the launch. Airlock records the integrator in a mapping rather than an event, so it is not recoverable from logs.

That the rate is stable over Doppler's life. It is not — the oldest blocks we swept run about 29 EOA launches to every 1 smart-account launch, which is why this is windowed at 30 days rather than measured all-time.

definitions.title: Share of all classified Doppler launches signed by a smart account
definitions.definition: The same measure as the 30-day rate, computed over every launch we have classified regardless of age.
definitions.method: Read the top-level `to` of each launch transaction; both ERC-4337 EntryPoint versions count as account abstraction.
excludes: Launches not yet classified.
does_not_assert: That this figure describes the layer today. It deliberately mixes eras — early Airlock launches run about 29 EOA to every 1 smart account, recent ones the other way — and is published only so the shift is visible beside the windowed number. Use the 30-day rate for anything current.

definitions.title: Blocking data-quality failures
definitions.definition: Checks of severity block that failed: while one of these fails, some published number is wrong.
definitions.method: Examples: an agent ranked L7+ with no countable payment behind it, a payment counted from before the agent existed, a published rate outside 0–1.
does_not_assert: Which number is wrong; read the check and its sample at /api/dq.

definitions.title: Data-quality checks run
definitions.definition: Number of assertion checks the data-quality suite ran over the tables every public number is computed from.
definitions.method: Each check is a SQL query that returns zero rows when the data is healthy. The catalogue, severities and thresholds are published at /api/dq.
excludes: Checks that exist only as ideas; a check counts once it runs on the timer.
does_not_assert: That the data is correct in ways no check tests. A passing suite is evidence against known failure shapes, not proof of truth.

definitions.title: Data-quality health score
definitions.definition: Weighted pass rate over block and warn checks.
definitions.method: Weight = dataset weight (tables the public rank is built from 3, published snapshots 2, partner tables 1) × severity (block 2, warn 1). Informational checks never move the score; a check that errors counts as failing.
excludes: Informational checks.
does_not_assert: Accuracy against the chain itself; it measures internal consistency and freshness.

definitions.title: Data-quality checks passing
definitions.definition: Checks in the latest run that returned zero failing rows.
definitions.method: Counted by the suite itself; informational checks that flag a known, expected shape (batch payments, shared operator wallets) count as not passing but never lower the health score.
does_not_assert: That a failing informational check is a defect.

definitions.title: Warning data-quality failures
definitions.definition: Checks of severity warn that failed: something is late or drifting, but published numbers are still correct.
definitions.method: Examples: a payment scan that has stalled, a promotion to L7 that has not happened yet.
does_not_assert: That a published number is wrong.

definitions.title: ERC-8004 registrations on Base
definitions.definition: Registrations on Base, as reported by the cited census.
definitions.method: Read from agenteconomy.to. Our own independent mint count for Base is published separately as registrations_minted_total; where they differ, both stand.
excludes: Other chains.
does_not_assert: That these are distinct operators, or live agents.

definitions.title: ERC-8004 registrations on BNB Smart Chain
definitions.definition: Registrations on BNB Smart Chain, as reported by the cited census.
definitions.method: Read from agenteconomy.to. Not reproduced — our own scans cover Base only.
excludes: Other chains.
does_not_assert: That these are distinct operators, or live agents. We have no independent measurement on this chain at all.

definitions.title: ERC-8004 registrations on Ethereum
definitions.definition: Registrations on Ethereum mainnet, as reported by the cited census.
definitions.method: Read from agenteconomy.to. Not reproduced — our own scans cover Base only.
excludes: Other chains.
does_not_assert: That these are distinct operators, or live agents. We have no independent measurement on this chain.

definitions.title: Share of registrations declaring an agent wallet
definitions.definition: Share of probed registrations whose descriptor names a wallet address the agent claims to control.
definitions.method: Read the parsed descriptor for a declared address. This is the join that makes everything downstream possible: without a declared wallet there is nothing to watch.
excludes: Registrations whose descriptor did not parse.
does_not_assert: That the agent controls the declared wallet. A declaration is a claim, and a claim is not a binding — which is why the binding record spec exists and why a declared wallet alone never raises an agent above L5.

definitions.title: Share of registrations declaring a protocol
definitions.definition: Share of registrations that name a protocol or capability in their record, as reported by the census source.
definitions.method: Read from the cited census. Not reproduced.
does_not_assert: That a declared protocol is implemented.

definitions.title: ERC-8004 registrations, per agenteconomy.to
definitions.definition: The registration count published by agenteconomy.to.
definitions.method: Read from their public interface. Not reproduced by us.
excludes: Whatever chains they do not index.
does_not_assert: That this is the number of agents.

That it agrees with 8004scan. The gap between the two is published as its own number, because a disagreement between sources is a fact about the sector rather than something to hide behind whichever figure we preferred.

definitions.title: ERC-8004 registrations, per 8004scan
definitions.definition: The registration count published by 8004scan.
definitions.method: Read from their public interface. Not reproduced by us.
excludes: Whatever chains they do not index.
does_not_assert: That this is the number of agents. It is the number of rows minted in a registry, and anyone can mint one.
That it agrees with the other census. It does not, by roughly an order of magnitude, and we publish both rather than choosing.

definitions.title: Disagreement between the two registration counts
definitions.definition: The difference between the two independent registration censuses.
definitions.method: Subtraction. Published deliberately: two sources counting the same registry and differing by this much is the single most useful caveat on any 'how many agents are there' claim.
does_not_assert: That one source is wrong. They count different chain sets and different inclusion rules, and neither publishes enough for us to adjudicate.
That the true figure lies between them.

definitions.title: USDC price in US dollars
definitions.definition: The market price of one USDC.
definitions.method: Read from CoinGecko.
does_not_assert: That USDC is worth a dollar. It is published precisely so a depeg would be visible rather than assumed away — every USD figure we compute from USDC amounts inherits this number.

definitions.title: Median USDC in a funded bound wallet
definitions.definition: The median balance among sampled bound wallets that hold USDC.
definitions.method: Median rather than mean, over funded wallets only.
excludes: Empty wallets, which would drag the median to zero and describe nothing.
does_not_assert: That a typical agent holds this. It is the middle of the funded ones, which are a minority.

definitions.title: Total USDC across sampled bound wallets
definitions.definition: The summed USDC balance of every bound wallet in the sample.
definitions.method: Balance reads, summed. USD conversion uses the published USDC price rather than an assumed dollar.
excludes: Other assets, other chains, and wallets outside the sample.
does_not_assert: That this is the agent economy's cash. It is a sample total, and the median beside it exists because a handful of wallets dominate the sum.

definitions.title: Bound wallets sampled
definitions.definition: How many agent-declared wallets the balance sweep read in this pass.
definitions.method: An even sample across Base registrations rather than the newest or the richest.
excludes: Wallets outside the sample, and registrations that declare no wallet.
does_not_assert: That the sample is the whole population. Rates computed from it are estimates with a stated denominator.

definitions.title: Share of bound wallets that hold money
definitions.definition: Funded bound wallets divided by bound wallets sampled.
definitions.method: Arithmetic on the two counts above, both from the same sweep so the denominator always matches the numerator.
excludes: The same exclusions as the two inputs.
does_not_assert: That the remainder are abandoned. It asserts that most declared agent wallets are empty at the moment we looked, which is a fact about readiness, not about intent.

definitions.title: Bound wallets holding money
definitions.definition: How many of the sampled bound wallets hold at least one dollar of USDC on Base.
definitions.method: Balance read per sampled wallet.
excludes: Balances in other assets and on other chains. A wallet funded entirely in ETH, or on another chain, counts as unfunded here.
does_not_assert: That an unfunded wallet is a dead agent. It may be funded just in time, or hold value we do not look at. It does mean the agent cannot pay from this address right now.

definitions.title: Actors in the graph
definitions.definition: Actor rows we hold — every registration we have sampled and joined, at any rung of the ladder.
definitions.method: Counted from our own store.
excludes: Registrations we have never sampled.
does_not_assert: That these are live agents. Most sit at the bottom of the ladder; the rung counts are published separately.

definitions.title: Open actor-to-wallet bindings
definitions.definition: Currently open bindings joining an actor to a wallet.
definitions.method: Counted from our own store. Closed bindings are retained as an audit trail and excluded here, so this is a present-tense count rather than a running total.
excludes: Closed bindings.
does_not_assert: That a binding proves control. It records the evidence we hold for the join; the strength of that evidence is what the ladder grades.

definitions.title: Payment rows recorded
definitions.definition: Every payment row we hold, including those excluded from published totals.
definitions.method: Counted from our own store. Deliberately larger than the published payment count: rows dated before their agent's registration are kept and flagged rather than deleted, so the exclusion is auditable.
does_not_assert: That every row counts toward observed volume. Roughly a quarter do not, and the excluded value is published as its own figure.

definitions.title: Endpoint probe results recorded
definitions.definition: Every endpoint probe result we have stored.
definitions.method: Counted from our own store. Failures are kept, not overwritten — a probe history is how the dead-endpoint detector works.
does_not_assert: That each probe is a distinct agent. One agent is probed repeatedly over time.

definitions.title: Wallets in the graph
definitions.definition: Distinct wallet addresses we hold a record for.
definitions.method: Counted from our own store.
excludes: Addresses we have never seen declared or paid.
does_not_assert: That each wallet belongs to a distinct party.

definitions.title: Time-series observations stored
definitions.definition: How many time-series observations the collector holds.
definitions.method: Counted from our own store. The archive published to the site is a downsample of this; the full resolution stays on the box.
does_not_assert: That every point is published. The public file keeps one point per day plus a 48-hour five-minute tail.

definitions.title: Funded agents that have not paid anyone
definitions.definition: Agents whose bound wallet holds at least $10 of USDC and which have made no countable payment to any counterparty in the last 7 days.
definitions.method: Latest balance read per bound wallet, against the most recent countable PAY per actor.
excludes: Agents with no balance read yet — absence of a reading is not evidence of an empty wallet.
does_not_assert: That the agent is broken or abandoned. A week of not paying is a week of not paying; some jobs are monthly.
That the balance is intended to be spent at all.

definitions.title: USDC held by idle funded agents
definitions.definition: Total USDC held by agents with at least $10 that have not paid anyone in seven days.
definitions.method: Balance of bound wallets joined against last observed payment. Both thresholds are stated choices, published so they can be argued with.
excludes: Agents below the balance threshold, and activity we cannot observe — an agent paying on another chain looks idle here.
does_not_assert: That the money is stranded or abandoned. It asserts that money is sitting next to an agent without moving, which is the gap between an agent economy existing and an agent economy running.

definitions.title: Live incidents
definitions.definition: Detections that are a harm AND recent: a retry loop burning an agent's money, a registration changing owner under a binding somebody relies on, or signing delegated to an implementation outside the curated allowlist, with an event time inside the last 72 hours.
definitions.method: Each hourly detector run closes any row that is not a harm kind or has aged out of the window, so the open flag means exactly this rule and nothing else. Mint bursts are never incidents.
excludes: Mint bursts, of any size. They measure a shape, not a harm.
Endpoints that never answer. That is a statement about our attempts, not damage done to anyone.
Anything older than 72 hours, which stays in the detection log.
does_not_assert: That zero means nothing bad is happening anywhere. It means none of these detectors has fired on a harm in what we measure.
That an incident is malicious. An identity changing owner can be a legitimate sale; it is an incident because anyone relying on the old owner is now exposed.

definitions.title: Open incidents
definitions.definition: Recorded events found by our detectors that remain open.
definitions.method: Queries over our own measurements. No external calls.
excludes: States. A low liveness score is a measurement, not an incident, and never appears here.
does_not_assert: That an incident is wrongdoing. A bulk minting burst is legitimate behaviour that changes what a registration count means.

definitions.title: Agents with income, 30 days
definitions.definition: Ranked agents with a counted income transfer dated in the last 30 days.
definitions.method: Distinct actor over money_events of kind EARN in the window.
excludes: Agents whose wallets the income scan has not read yet.
does_not_assert: That the agent earned the money.

definitions.title: Agents with income
definitions.definition: Ranked agents with at least one counted income transfer.
definitions.method: Distinct actor over money_events of kind EARN.
excludes: Agents whose wallets the income scan has not read yet.
does_not_assert: That the agent earned the money.

definitions.title: Income transfers
definitions.window: all time since each registration's mint block
definitions.definition: Counted stablecoin transfers into ranked agents (income.usd.total.v1 rules).
definitions.method: Count over money_events of kind EARN.
excludes: Everything income.usd.total.v1 excludes.
does_not_assert: That each transfer is a sale.

definitions.title: Net flow, 30 days
definitions.definition: Agent income over the window (income.usd.total.v1 rules) minus counted agent spending over the window (pay.usd.total.v1 rules).
definitions.method: Two sums over money_events, kinds EARN and PAY, same exclusions.
excludes: Everything either side excludes.
does_not_assert: Profitability. Income includes operator top-ups; spending includes purchases the operator intended.

definitions.title: Addresses that paid agents
definitions.definition: Distinct senders of counted income transfers into ranked agents.
definitions.method: Distinct from-address over money_events of kind EARN.
does_not_assert: That a payer is a customer. An operator funding its own agent is a payer here.

definitions.title: Agent income, 30 days
definitions.definition: Agent income (income.usd.total.v1 rules) dated in the last 30 days.
definitions.method: Sum over money_events of kind EARN, same exclusions.
excludes: Everything income.usd.total.v1 excludes.
does_not_assert: That the money paid for work rather than funding the agent.

definitions.title: Agent income
definitions.window: all time since each registration's mint block
definitions.definition: The summed USD value of stablecoin transfers INTO a wallet bound to a ranked registration (USDC, USDT, EURC at the day's rate, DAI), from a different address, after the registration existed.
definitions.method: alchemy_getAssetTransfers with toAddress over every ranked wallet, each re-read about twice a week; the same receipt check as spending marks money that arrived and left in one transaction as a hop.
excludes: Transfers dated before the registration's mint block.
Money that left again in the same transaction (a hop or a swap).
Self-transfers.
Wallets not yet read: the count is a floor while the first pass runs.
does_not_assert: That the transfer paid for the agent's work rather than funding it: an operator topping up a wallet is income here too. Payers that are themselves ranked agents are the closest thing to earned revenue, and are separable by address.

definitions.title: Anomalous daily move
definitions.window: 30 complete days of trailing baseline, minimum 20 observations
definitions.definition: A metric whose latest complete-day observation lies at least two standard deviations from the mean of its own trailing baseline, AND whose move clears a per-metric absolute floor.
definitions.method: The statistic depends on how the metric moves: a cumulative counter is differenced to a daily increment, a level becomes a day-over-day percentage change, a rate becomes a percentage-point change, and a daily flow is used as-is. Guessing a family would be worse than silence, so a metric with no declared family is never tested.
excludes: The current UTC day, always — a partial day against a full-day baseline is a different measurement, not a small error.
Metrics with fewer than 20 baseline observations.
does_not_assert: Causation, or that the move is news. It says the number is unusual for itself, which is the only thing statistics can say.
That an unflagged day was uneventful — a move can be real and still sit inside two sigma of a volatile series.

definitions.title: Share of delegated agent wallets on an allowlisted implementation
definitions.definition: Delegated bound wallets pointing at an implementation on our published allowlist, divided by all delegated bound wallets.
definitions.method: Read the 7702 designator from each wallet's code and match the implementation address against the allowlist file.
excludes: Wallets whose code we have not read.
does_not_assert: That non-allowlisted implementations are malicious. The allowlist ships EMPTY on purpose: an implementation nobody has read is unknown rather than untrusted, so this figure reads zero by design until somebody does the reading.
Safety. An allowlisted implementation can still be used badly.

definitions.title: Delegated bound agent wallets
definitions.definition: Bound wallets whose on-chain code is the EIP-7702 designator followed by an implementation address.
definitions.method: Read exactly from the wallet's code. Nothing else produces that byte pattern.
excludes: Wallets whose code we have not read.
does_not_assert: Risk. Delegation is the intended mechanism, not a defect.

definitions.title: Visible externally-owned bound wallets
definitions.definition: Bound wallets we have examined that carry no code at all.
definitions.method: Counted only over wallets whose code we have actually read.
excludes: Wallets never examined.
does_not_assert: That these wallets are unsafe. It asserts that whatever policy governs them is not enforced on-chain, which is a different and narrower statement.

definitions.title: Float share of the top 7702 implementation
definitions.definition: USDC held by delegated bound wallets pointing at the single most common implementation, divided by USDC held by all delegated bound wallets.
definitions.method: Weighted by float rather than by wallet count, because blast radius is money and not headcount.
excludes: Wallets whose code we have not read, and assets other than USDC.
does_not_assert: That the implementation is at risk. It says how much money would be affected if it were.
That a wallet-count share would look the same. It usually does not: ten dust wallets are not one funded one.

definitions.title: Share of delegated agent wallets on an unrecognised implementation
definitions.definition: One minus the allowlisted share.
definitions.method: Derived from the same single query, so the two cannot disagree.
excludes: Wallets whose code we have not read.
does_not_assert: That the implementations are dangerous. Unknown means unread, and reading them is work nobody has published.

definitions.title: USDC float on wallets we have watched pay
definitions.definition: USDC held across wallets bound to an actor at liveness 7 or above.
definitions.method: Balances read on the keyless public mesh through Multicall3, batched 50 wallets per call.
excludes: Wallets we have not bound, and every asset other than USDC on Base.
does_not_assert: USDC held by agents in general. It is a floor over the agents WE bound and observed, and the true figure is larger by an unknown amount.
That this money is destined to be spent. It is float, which is the point of measuring it separately from payments.

definitions.title: Fetch / Almanac identities attempted
definitions.definition: Almanac identities we have ingested from the Agentverse search API and run our qualifier against.
definitions.method: The search index caps any single query at 10,000 results, so we rotate a term list and page through each. Every row records which term produced it.
excludes: Almanac rows we have not reached yet. This is our attempted set, not their registry.
does_not_assert: That this is the size of the Almanac. It is the size of what we have checked, which is the only denominator a reader can reproduce.
That the sample is uniform. The term list is deliberately weighted toward money — wallet, usdc, x402, treasury — which biases the bind rate UPWARD. A uniform sample would return a lower figure.

definitions.title: Fetch / Almanac bind rate
definitions.definition: Bound identities divided by attempted identities.
definitions.method: One query, so both counts come from the same instant. Reading a numerator and a denominator from separate queries during an active ingest once published a negative ratio.
excludes: Identities we have not attempted.
does_not_assert: A ceiling on how many Almanac agents handle money. It is a floor on how many we could pay, which is a narrower claim.
That the rate is unbiased. Our sampling deliberately favours money-related agents, so this figure is an upper bound.

definitions.title: Fetch / Almanac identities bound to a payable wallet
definitions.definition: Attempted Almanac identities for which we found an EVM address in the agent card, and which do not share that address with another identity in the same catalog.
definitions.method: Scan the agent card for an EVM address, excluding burn addresses. An Almanac identity is itself a Fetch-chain bech32 address and cannot receive USDC on Base.
excludes: Fetch-chain addresses, which are a different money object.
Identities sharing a declared wallet with another identity.
does_not_assert: That unbound agents are fake or inactive. It asserts only that nothing in their card tells us where to pay them on Base.
That Fetch-native spending does not exist. It does, and it would be published as its own series rather than folded into a Base figure.

definitions.title: Fetch / Almanac wallets that moved USDC
definitions.definition: Bound Almanac wallets observed sending USDC to a different address after the identity existed.
definitions.method: Same asset-transfer read as every other catalog. Self-transfers and burn addresses excluded.
excludes: Self-transfers.
Fetch-chain activity.
does_not_assert: L7. See partner.virtuals.moved.v1 for why an outbound transfer is not a payment for work.

definitions.title: Almanac identities Agentverse itself marks active, in our sample
definitions.definition: Identities in our ingested Fetch sample whose Agentverse status is active — their reachability object, counted on our rows.
definitions.method: Read from their own status field. Published beside our bind rate so the two objects sit on the same sample.
excludes: Almanac rows we have not ingested.
does_not_assert: Our L5. Their active means reachable and unexpired on their infrastructure; ours means an endpoint answered our probe. The two are allowed to disagree and are never merged.
A judgement about their registry. It is their number, on our sample, so a reader can see both objects at once.

definitions.title: Virtuals identities attempted
definitions.definition: Virtuals agent identities we have ingested from the public catalog API and run our qualifier against.
definitions.method: Paged through the public catalog, a few hundred per run, advancing a cursor so the set grows visibly over days rather than arriving as one unverifiable dump.
excludes: Catalog rows we have not reached yet.
does_not_assert: That this is the size of the Virtuals catalog. It is the size of what we have checked.

definitions.title: Virtuals identities their catalog marks launched
definitions.definition: Identities in our ingested set whose status in the Virtuals catalog is AVAILABLE — launched and tradeable.
definitions.method: Read from their own status field on our own rows. Their object, counted on our sample.
excludes: Identities we have not ingested.
does_not_assert: That a launched agent is a working agent. Launch is a token event.
Our own liveness. This is their status field, published beside ours so a reader can see the two are answers to different questions.

definitions.title: Virtuals bind rate
definitions.definition: Bound identities divided by attempted identities.
definitions.method: One query, so numerator and denominator come from the same instant.
excludes: Identities we have not attempted.
Identities on a shared wallet, which are excluded from the numerator.
does_not_assert: That a bound agent is a live agent. Binding is a join and nothing more.

definitions.title: Virtuals identities bound to a sole-declarant wallet
definitions.definition: Attempted Virtuals identities declaring an agent wallet, or an ERC-6551 token-bound account where no agent wallet is declared, which no other identity in the same catalog also declares.
definitions.method: Take the declared agent wallet first, then the token-bound account. The token address is recorded as an attribute and never bound.
excludes: Token addresses. Holders are fans, not operators.
Identities sharing a wallet with another identity in the same catalog — one address in this catalog is declared by 84 different agents.
does_not_assert: That each bound identity is a distinct operator. Same-funder clustering across DISTINCT wallets is not applied yet, so read this as an upper bound.
That a bound wallet has done anything. Binding is a join, not evidence of activity.

definitions.title: Virtuals identities carrying a token address
definitions.definition: Identities in our ingested set with a deployed token address — registration on the token rail.
definitions.method: Presence of tokenAddress in the catalog record. Recorded as an attribute and NEVER used as a binding.
excludes: Pre-launch identities, which have no token yet.
does_not_assert: Value, revenue or capital at work. A token address is a contract, and its holders are fans rather than operators.
That the agent can be paid. The token address is not a wallet and we never bind to one.

definitions.title: Virtuals identities carrying an ACP identity
definitions.definition: Identities in our ingested set that declare an Agent Commerce Protocol agent id — registration on the job rail.
definitions.method: Presence of acpAgentId or v3AcpAgentId in the catalog record.
excludes: Identities with a token address but no ACP id, counted separately.
does_not_assert: That a job was sold, requested, evaluated or settled. It is a registration on a job protocol, not a transaction on one — we do not ingest ACP job state yet.
That the agent is live. An ACP id is a name on a second rail, and a name is not a worker.

definitions.title: Virtuals moved-USDC rate, alternate id
definitions.definition: Retained identifier for the moved-USDC rate over wallets read, kept so that series rows written before the metric was renamed still resolve.
definitions.method: Superseded by partner.virtuals.moved_rate.v1. The figure is identical; only the name changed, because the old one implied an L7 claim the measurement does not support.
excludes: Nothing additional.
does_not_assert: L7, despite the identifier. The rename exists precisely because the original name over-claimed.

definitions.title: Most Virtuals identities from one operator
definitions.definition: The largest number of ingested identities sharing a single creator account id.
definitions.method: Group by the catalog's own creator account id and take the maximum.
excludes: Rows with no operator key yet, which is why this figure only rises.
does_not_assert: Wrongdoing. A prolific creator is a prolific creator.
A final value. It grows as coverage grows, which is why it is a live figure rather than a sentence.

definitions.title: Most Virtuals identities declaring one single wallet
definitions.definition: The largest number of Virtuals identities in our ingested set that declare the same wallet address.
definitions.method: Group declarations by address within the partner's own catalog and take the maximum.
excludes: Identities we have not ingested yet, which is why this figure only ever rises.
does_not_assert: Wrongdoing. Launching many agents from one wallet is ordinary; this measures a naming habit, not a deception.

A final value. It was 84 when first measured on a small sample and grows as we read further into the catalog, which is exactly why it is published as a live figure rather than written into a sentence.

definitions.title: Virtuals wallets that moved USDC after launch
definitions.definition: Bound Virtuals wallets observed sending USDC to a DIFFERENT address at or after the identity's own launch date.
definitions.method: One asset-transfer read per wallet, capped per run. Self-transfers and burn addresses are excluded; transfers timestamped before the identity's launch are excluded and counted separately.
excludes: Self-transfers — moving your own money between your own wallets is not paying anybody.
Everything the wallet did before the agent existed. A declared wallet is frequently years older than the agent declared on it.
does_not_assert: L7. This is deliberately NOT our liveness rung. From a raw wallet read, a token launch, a bonding-curve buy, a liquidity add and a DEX swap are all outbound USDC transfers, and we cannot yet separate them from a payment for work.
That the counterparty was another agent, or that any service was delivered.

definitions.title: Virtuals moved-USDC rate over wallets read
definitions.definition: Wallets that moved USDC after launch, divided by the bound wallets we have actually read on-chain.
definitions.method: Denominator is wallets READ, not wallets bound. While a sweep is working through a catalog of tens of thousands, a rate over the bound set would mostly measure how far the sweep has got.
excludes: Bound wallets not yet read.
does_not_assert: A liveness rate. See partner.virtuals.moved.v1 for what this counts and what it refuses to claim.

definitions.title: Distinct operators behind Virtuals identities
definitions.definition: Distinct creator account ids across the ingested identities where the catalog supplies one.
definitions.method: The platform's own creator account id — an exact same-operator key, not an inference from funding patterns. ONLY the opaque integer is stored: the catalog returns an email address, a username and social handles beside it, and none of those enter this graph.
excludes: Rows ingested before 2026-09-12, when we began recording the key. Those backfill as the cursor cycles.
does_not_assert: That this is the number of operators on the platform. It is the number among rows where WE know the key — published beside `operator_known` so the coverage is never hidden.
That one operator running many agents is improper. It is ordinary, and it is the reason a name count and an actor count diverge.

definitions.title: Identities per operator
definitions.definition: Rows with a known creator account, divided by the distinct creator accounts among them.
definitions.method: Computed only over rows where the operator is known, so a partially backfilled set cannot flatter it.
excludes: Rows with no operator key yet.
does_not_assert: A catalog-wide ratio, until coverage approaches the full set. Read it against `operator_known` — both are published in the same block for that reason.
That the identities are duplicates. They are distinct agents; they share a person.

definitions.title: Virtuals wallets with USDC history predating their agent
definitions.definition: Bound Virtuals wallets whose observed outbound USDC transfers include at least one timestamped BEFORE the identity's own launch date.
definitions.method: Compare each transfer's block timestamp against the identity's launch or creation date from the catalog.
excludes: Wallets whose entire history postdates their agent.
does_not_assert: Deception. People declare wallets they already had, which is ordinary.
That the pre-launch money was an agent's. It was a person's, which is exactly why it is excluded from every other figure — counting it once overstated our own published headline by 46%.

definitions.title: Virtuals bound wallets read on-chain
definitions.definition: Bound Virtuals wallets whose transfer history we have actually read.
definitions.method: Capped per run and paced against the provider budget, oldest check first.
excludes: Bound wallets still queued for a read.
does_not_assert: That unread wallets are inactive. They are unread, and every rate we publish over this set says so.

definitions.title: Virtuals shared-wallet rate
definitions.definition: The share of Virtuals identities declaring a wallet that at least one other identity in the same catalog also declares.
definitions.method: Group declarations by address within the partner's own catalog; any address with more than one declarant marks all of them.
excludes: Identities that declare no wallet at all.
does_not_assert: Wrongdoing. Launching many agents from one wallet is ordinary, and this measures a naming habit rather than a deception.
That the identities are related to each other in any other way. It says only that several names point at one address.

definitions.title: Virtuals identities still pre-graduation
definitions.definition: Identities in our ingested set whose status is UNDERGRAD — they have not graduated from the bonding curve.
definitions.method: Their own status field, counted on our rows.
excludes: Identities we have not ingested.
does_not_assert: Failure. Most of a launchpad catalog being pre-launch is what a launchpad looks like.
That these agents will never work. It says they have not started, which is why every rate over the whole catalog must be read against this number.
