definitions.title: Our coverage of the x402 rail
definitions.definition: Distinct x402 payers we observe, divided by the unique-payer count a public x402 index reports for the same chain.
definitions.method: Numerator is ours: bound wallets we watched pay a known x402 recipient. Denominator is somebody else's published figure, cited rather than reproduced.
excludes: x402 activity by payers we have not bound.
does_not_assert: That our payer classes describe the rail. They describe our slice, and this number exists to say how small that slice is.
That the two figures are the same object. Ours is cumulative over bound wallets; theirs is a 24-hour unique-payer count.

definitions.title: x402 payers in a same-minter cluster
definitions.definition: Observed x402 payers whose ERC-8004 registration was minted by an address that minted 25 or more registrations.
definitions.method: Join the payer's registration to the registry's own mint records and group by minter.
excludes: Payers with no ERC-8004 registration, who cannot be clustered this way at all.
does_not_assert: Fraud, sybil intent, or wrongdoing. It is a shape in the data: many registrations from one address. Bulk minting is legal and often mundane.
That members of a cluster are controlled by one party today. Registrations are transferable.

definitions.title: x402 payers with independent payment evidence
definitions.definition: Observed x402 payers that also have a verified payment made BEFORE their first x402 ticket, or to a counterparty that is not an x402 recipient.
definitions.method: The ticket being classified may not be the evidence that promotes its own payer. Without that rule every farm that pays once becomes a labelled live agent.
excludes: Evidence consisting only of the x402 tickets under classification.
does_not_assert: That unlabelled payers are farms. They are unlabelled, which means we have not joined them to an identity.

definitions.title: x402 payers we observe
definitions.definition: Distinct bound wallets we have watched pay a known x402 recipient address.
definitions.method: Join our own verified payments against the harvested x402 recipient set.
excludes: x402 payers we have not bound to an identity, which is almost all of them.
does_not_assert: The number of x402 payers on Base. See partner.x402.coverage.v1 for how small a slice this is.

definitions.title: x402 tickets we observe
definitions.definition: Verified payments from bound wallets that landed on a known x402 recipient address.
definitions.method: Counted alongside unique payers on purpose: farms retry, so a ticket share always looks worse than a payer share.
excludes: Payments to x402 recipients we have not harvested.
does_not_assert: Total x402 volume. This is our observed slice and it is a floor.

definitions.title: Counted payments carrying an app's Builder Code
definitions.window: all time; transactions are read once
definitions.definition: Counted payments whose transaction carries an ERC-8021 Builder Code: a suffix appended to the calldata by the app, wallet or agent framework that built the transaction. Reported as the USD attributed, the number of distinct codes, and the largest code's share of attributed USD.
definitions.method: The transaction input is read from the public Base RPC and its ERC-8021 suffix parsed (schema 0: ASCII codes). Codes are registered in the Base Builder Codes registry (0x000000BC7E6457e610fe52Dcc0ca5b3ce59C8E80).
excludes: Transactions not yet read (reported as pending in the note).
Suffixes in schemas other than 0, which are counted but not decoded.
does_not_assert: Who operates an app: a code names an app that attributed itself, and its registered metadata is usually private.
That payments without a code were not made through an app.

definitions.title: Distinct addresses agents have paid
definitions.definition: Distinct recipient addresses across all observed agent payments.
definitions.method: Counted from the same payment set, after the pre-registration exclusion.
excludes: Recipients of excluded payments.
does_not_assert: That each address is a distinct seller. Most are contracts, and one operator can run many.
That we know what any of them do. Where we can name one from a citable source we publish the label; most remain unnamed.

definitions.title: Observed agent payments
definitions.definition: USDC transfers we have watched leave a wallet bound to a tracked agent, dated after that agent's registration.
definitions.method: Asset-transfer scan per bound wallet. Every payment is dated against the mint date of its agent's registration, and anything earlier is held out of this count.
excludes: Transfers from before the agent existed. Counting those inflated our own headline by roughly three times before we read mint dates.
Inferred payments. If we did not observe the transfer, it is not here.
Assets other than USDC, and chains other than Base.
does_not_assert: That this is all agent payment activity. It is what we can see from wallets we have bound, which is a sample.
That each payment was autonomous. We observe a transfer, not the decision behind it.

definitions.title: Pass-through USD excluded from agent spending
definitions.definition: USD value of outgoing USDC transfers from agent-bound wallets that were routing hops: money that arrived and left again on its way somewhere else, rather than the agent paying for something.
definitions.method: Each observed payment is checked against the wallet's own inflows; a transfer that forwards funds it just received is marked pass_through and excluded from every spending total. The excluded amount is published so the exclusion can be audited, not just trusted.
excludes: Payments from before the agent was registered, which are excluded separately (pay.excluded.preregistration.v1).
does_not_assert: That pass-through money is illegitimate. Routing is a normal thing for a wallet to do; it is just not the agent spending.

definitions.title: Payment value excluded as pre-registration
definitions.definition: Value moved by bound wallets BEFORE the registration they are bound to was minted, and therefore excluded from every published payment figure.
definitions.method: Each registration's mint block is read from the Identity registry's ERC-721 mint. Any transfer earlier than that block is marked and stops counting.
does_not_assert: That these payments are illegitimate. They are simply not agent payments — they happened before the agent existed.

definitions.title: Circular payments in the counted set
definitions.definition: Wallet pairs that paid each other in both directions within the counted set, the USD matched in both directions (the smaller of the two sums for each pair), and counted payments whose recipient is itself a wallet bound to an ERC-8004 identity.
definitions.method: Self-join of counted payments on sender and recipient.
excludes: Loops that pass through wallets we do not watch.
does_not_assert: That reciprocal payments are wash trading: two agents can legitimately buy from each other.

definitions.title: Share of observed value from the largest single actor
definitions.definition: The fraction of total observed payment value contributed by the single actor with the greatest observed value.
definitions.method: max(sum(amount_usd) grouped by actor) divided by the countable total.
excludes: The same exclusions as pay.usd.total.v1.
does_not_assert: That the largest actor is anomalous or wrong. It is published so the total can be read honestly, not to cast doubt on it.

definitions.title: Counted payments less own positions
definitions.window: all time since each registration's mint block
definitions.definition: Counted payment value minus pay.usd.ownpositions.v1: what left the paying wallet's control on Base.
definitions.method: observed_pay_usd_total minus observed_pay_usd_own_positions, computed in the same run.
excludes: Deposits proven to be credited to the payer.
does_not_assert: That all of it bought goods or services: bridged money may reach the same owner on another chain, and a swap exchanges one asset for another.
Precision beyond the receipt check: lending and vault payments not yet checked stay in this figure until they are, so it is an upper bound on what left.

definitions.title: Median observed payment
definitions.definition: The median USD value of a single countable observed payment.
definitions.method: percentile_cont(0.5) over amount_usd of countable PAY events.
excludes: The same exclusions as pay.usd.total.v1.
does_not_assert: That payments are distributed symmetrically. They are not: the mean is several times the median.

definitions.title: Counted payments into the payer's own positions
definitions.window: all time since each registration's mint block
definitions.definition: The part of the counted payment value that went into a lending market or vault position credited to the paying wallet itself: in the same transaction the payer is minted the position's claim token (vault shares, aTokens), or the market sends the payer its own token.
definitions.method: For counted payments to recipients labelled lending or yield_vault (policy adapters included), the transaction receipt is read once and searched for an ERC-20 Transfer to the payer from the zero address, or from the recipient contract of its own token. Receipts from the public Base RPC.
excludes: Swaps: a token bought is an exchange, not a position in a market.
Bridges: money that leaves Base may still be the agent's, but a receipt on Base cannot show it.
Deposits whose receipt credits someone other than the payer.
does_not_assert: That the agent still holds the position today: withdrawals are separate inflows and can follow minutes later.
Anything about who operates the wallets, the adapter or the markets.

definitions.title: Observed payment value
definitions.window: all time since each registration's mint block
definitions.definition: The summed USD value of every countable observed payment out of a bound wallet.
definitions.method: Sum of amount_usd over money_events of kind PAY where pre_registration is false.
excludes: Pre-registration payments (see pay.excluded.preregistration.v1).
Payments from wallets whose registration has no mint date yet — held out until dated, never assumed.
does_not_assert: That this is the size of the agent economy. It is a sample: what we watched, from the wallets we have bound, on one chain, in one asset.
That the total is typical of its members — read pay.topactor.share.v1 and pay.usd.median.v1 beside it.

definitions.title: Share of descriptors on a shared host
definitions.definition: Share of probed registrations whose URI points at a hosting service shared by many other registrations rather than at their own domain.
definitions.method: Group resolved URIs by host and mark hosts carrying many distinct registrations.
excludes: Registrations with no resolvable URI.
does_not_assert: That shared hosting is illegitimate. It is cheap and sensible. It does mean a single host outage can take a large slice of the registry offline at once, and that concentration is worth seeing.

definitions.title: L1 — registration declares a URI
definitions.definition: Share of probed registrations whose on-chain record contains a non-empty URI.
definitions.method: Read the registration's stored URI and check it is not blank.
excludes: Registrations we could not read at all.
does_not_assert: That the URI resolves, or that anything is behind it. That is the next rung, and most of the fall-off happens there.

definitions.title: L2 — the URI answers
definitions.definition: Share of probed registrations whose declared URI returns a 2xx response.
definitions.method: One HTTP request per registration, with a timeout. A timeout is a failure, not a retry-until-success.
excludes: Registrations with no URI to fetch.
does_not_assert: That the response is an agent card, or valid, or truthful. A 200 from a parked domain counts here and fails the next rung.

definitions.title: L3 — the document parses
definitions.definition: Share of probed registrations whose URI returns a document that parses as the expected agent descriptor.
definitions.method: Parse the response and check the required shape is present.
excludes: Registrations that never answered.
does_not_assert: That the contents are accurate. Schema validity means somebody filled in the right fields, not that the fields are true.

definitions.title: L4 — the agent declares services
definitions.definition: Share of probed registrations whose descriptor declares at least one service or endpoint it offers.
definitions.method: Read the parsed descriptor and look for a non-empty service declaration.
excludes: Registrations whose document did not parse.
does_not_assert: That the service works, or is reachable, or has ever been paid for. Declaring a service is a claim by the operator; the ladder does not treat it as evidence of trade.

definitions.title: Live endpoint rate
definitions.definition: Share of a uniform random sample of registrations whose declared service endpoint returned a successful response to a plain GET.
definitions.method: Uniform random sample over the registry's token id space, then an HTTP probe with an 8 s timeout, at most 2 redirects, a 256 KB body cap, and no execution of anything returned.
excludes: Registrations whose only endpoint is a shared hosting platform's submit URL — that proves the platform is up and nothing about the agent. Those cap at L4.
does_not_assert: That the agent behind the endpoint works, only that something answered.

definitions.title: Registrations probed
definitions.definition: How many registrations the endpoint sweep actually tested.
definitions.method: An even sample across the registry rather than the newest or the busiest, so the ladder rates below describe the registry rather than its most active corner.
excludes: Registrations outside the sample.
does_not_assert: That the sample is large enough for any particular subgroup. It supports registry-wide rates, not per-operator claims.

definitions.title: What the ranks cost to reach
definitions.definition: Ranked identities (L7 and above) whose counted payments sum to less than one US dollar, and the smallest counted total among L9 identities.
definitions.method: Sum of counted payments per ranked identity. Zero-value transfers, which anyone can emit from any address, are checked separately and are not in the counted set.
excludes: Payments outside the counted set.
does_not_assert: That a small total is fake: x402 micropayments are legitimately a fraction of a cent.
That the rank rules will change; this measures how cheap each rung is today.

definitions.title: Actor at liveness 7 or above
definitions.window: all time since the registration's mint block
definitions.definition: An ERC-8004 registration for which we have observed at least one non-inferred outbound stablecoin payment, from a wallet bound to that registration, to a DIFFERENT address.
definitions.method: alchemy_getAssetTransfers over the stablecoins on Base (USDC; and since 27 September 2026 USDT, EURC and DAI, with EURC converted at the day's EURC/USD), filtered to transfers out of a bound wallet, plus Alchemy address-activity pushes for ranked wallets. The binding comes from ownerOf() on the Identity registry, or from an agentWallet declared in the registration file. Each payment carries its asset on the record.
excludes: Self-transfers — moving your own money between your own wallets is not paying a counterparty.
Any payment whose block time precedes the registration's mint block. A wallet may have been a person's for years before it was bound to an agent.
Payments by an actor whose registration has since changed hands, from the moment the binding closes.
does_not_assert: That the agent is autonomous. We cannot see whether a human approved the payment.
That the wallet is controlled by the registrant, only that it is bound by one of the recorded methods.
Anything about what the payment was for.

definitions.title: Actor at liveness 8 or above
definitions.definition: Everything rank.l7plus.v1 requires, and the paying wallet still holds at least $10 of USDC at our most recent balance read.
definitions.method: USDC balanceOf via Multicall3 over every ranked wallet, every six hours, and again at the moment an evidence pack is bought.
excludes: Wallets whose balance we have not read.
Non-USDC holdings. USDT, EURC and DAI balances are read alongside and published on the record as stables_float and float_breakdown, but the L8 line is still USDC until this definition is versioned.
does_not_assert: That the balance is the agent's operating budget, or that anyone intends to spend it.

definitions.title: Actor at liveness 9
definitions.window: rolling 30 days for the counterparty count
definitions.definition: Everything rank.l8plus.v1 requires, and payments to three or more DISTINCT counterparty addresses within the last 30 days.
definitions.method: Distinct to-addresses over the window, counted from observed transfers.
excludes: Repeat payments to the same address, which count once however often they recur.
does_not_assert: That the counterparties are unrelated to each other or to the agent.

definitions.title: Time from registration to first counted payment
definitions.window: from each identity's mint to the time of measurement
definitions.definition: The probability that an ERC-8004 identity on Base has made its first counted payment within t days of its mint, estimated with the Kaplan-Meier product-limit estimator; identities that have not paid are censored at the time of measurement.
definitions.method: Mint time from the registry (or the dated census); first payment is the earliest counted payment. Cohorts by the minting address's total mints on Base: single (1), 2-9, 10-99, 100-999, 1000 and more. Published at 365 days, with the median days to a first payment among identities that paid.
excludes: Identities without a mint time.
Payments excluded from the counted set (pre-registration, routing hops).
does_not_assert: That an identity that has not paid is idle: it may pay from a wallet we have not bound.
Why burst-minted identities pay less often; only that they do.

definitions.title: Hours containing a minting burst
definitions.definition: How many distinct address-hours met the burst threshold.
definitions.method: Counted alongside the registrations above.
does_not_assert: That each burst is a separate operator or a separate incident.

definitions.title: Share of the registry that arrived in bursts
definitions.definition: Burst-minted registrations divided by all registrations minted.
definitions.method: Arithmetic on the two counts above.
excludes: The same undercount at hour boundaries.
does_not_assert: That the remainder was organic. It is a floor on scripted minting, not a measure of authenticity.

definitions.title: Registrations minted in bursts
definitions.definition: Registrations minted as part of a run of 25 or more from a single address inside one hour.
definitions.method: Group mints by address and hour; count those in hours meeting the threshold. The threshold is a stated choice, not a natural boundary — it is published so a reader can disagree with it.
excludes: Bursts spread across an hour boundary, which this undercounts.
does_not_assert: That burst-minted registrations are worthless. They are the signature of a script rather than of people signing up one at a time, and that distinction matters when the registry count is quoted as adoption.

definitions.title: Registrations minted on Base
definitions.definition: Every ERC-8004 Identity registration ever minted on Base, counted from the registry's own ERC-721 mint transfers, each with the exact block it landed in.
definitions.method: alchemy_getAssetTransfers over the Identity contract, category erc721, transfers from the zero address.
excludes: Other chains. Public counters that report a much larger number are summing several chains.
does_not_assert: That this is a count of agents. It is a count of names issued — see reg.transferred.v1 and reg.burstminted.rate.v1 for why those differ.

definitions.title: Registrations minted per day
definitions.definition: The number of ERC-8004 registrations minted on Base during a complete UTC day, counted from the registry's own ERC-721 mint transfers.
definitions.method: Grouped from the mint block timestamp of every registration we have dated. The current day is never published: a day's count is not a fact until the day is over.
excludes: The running current day.
Other chains.
does_not_assert: That the registrations represent distinct operators — see the minting-concentration finding, where one address accounts for an eighth of the registry.
definitions.supersedes_in_practice: A cited daily feed we previously relied on, which froze at the same value for two consecutive days while the chain kept moving.

definitions.title: Distinct addresses that minted registrations
definitions.definition: How many distinct addresses have minted at least one registration.
definitions.method: Group mints by recipient address. The address set behind this is published in full.
excludes: Chains other than Base.
does_not_assert: That each address is a distinct person or company. One operator can mint from many addresses, which would make the concentration below an understatement rather than an overstatement.

definitions.title: Share of the registry minted by ten addresses
definitions.definition: Registrations minted by the ten busiest addresses, divided by all registrations minted.
definitions.method: As above, taking the top ten.
does_not_assert: That the ten are unrelated to each other.

definitions.title: Share of the registry minted by one address
definitions.definition: Registrations minted by the single busiest address, divided by all registrations minted.
definitions.method: Group mints by address, take the largest, divide by the total.
does_not_assert: That those registrations are fake. Bulk minting is legitimate for a platform issuing identities on behalf of users. It does mean the headline registry count is not a count of independent participants, and reading it as one is the mistake this number exists to prevent.

definitions.title: Share of registrations that have changed hands
definitions.definition: Registrations that have been transferred at least once, divided by all registrations minted.
definitions.method: Distinct transferred token ids over the mint count.
excludes: Transfers we have not swept yet.
does_not_assert: That an identity was sold to a new operator. A transferable identity means a reputation history can change owner without any signal to the people relying on it — that is the reason to publish this, not a claim that it has happened commercially.

definitions.title: Registrations that changed hands
definitions.definition: Registrations transferred at least once after minting — a secondary transfer, not a mint.
definitions.method: Same sweep as reg.minted.base.v1; transfers whose from-address is not the zero address.
excludes: Mints.
does_not_assert: That the agent changed. Only that the holder did.

definitions.title: Registration transfer events
definitions.definition: Secondary transfers of registration tokens — moves after the original mint.
definitions.method: Read from the Identity registry's own transfer log, excluding mints.
excludes: Mints, which are counted separately.
does_not_assert: That a transfer is a sale. It could be a custody move between wallets of the same operator, and nothing on-chain distinguishes the two.

definitions.title: Registrations that have received feedback
definitions.definition: Distinct registrations with at least one on-chain feedback event against them.
definitions.method: Read from the ERC-8004 Reputation registry's own logs on the keyless Base mesh.
excludes: Feedback on chains we do not scan.
does_not_assert: That a rated agent is a real or active one. Ten addresses wrote half of all feedback, much of it covering agents they cannot plausibly have transacted with.

definitions.title: Feedback events in the last 24 hours
definitions.definition: Feedback events recorded in the last day.
definitions.method: Counted from our own ingest. Withheld entirely while the scan is behind the chain head — mid-backfill this measures how far we have read rather than what happened, and publishing that zero would be a false statement about the world.
excludes: Events in blocks we have not reached.
does_not_assert: That the day's activity is organic.

definitions.title: On-chain agent feedback events
definitions.window: all time since the registry's first event
definitions.definition: Feedback events emitted by the ERC-8004 Reputation registry, read from the registry's own logs.
definitions.method: Log scan over the keyless public Base mesh, which serves 10,000-block ranges where the paid tier caps at ten. No ABI was published, so the event layout was recovered from real logs: the rated agent id and the rater address are indexed topics, followed by two tag strings and two URIs.
excludes: Events on other chains.
Any field whose meaning the bytes do not make unambiguous.
does_not_assert: That feedback is true, earned, or disinterested. It is somebody's opinion published on-chain, and it can be bought as easily as it can be earned.
That the numeric fields are scores. One ranges from 5 to 1e20 across observed events — the shape of a token amount, not a rating — so it is published unnamed rather than guessed at.
That a rated agent is a working agent. Rating and observed payment are independent facts; the overlap between them is published separately.
definitions.note: Reputation is a SIGNAL and carries no weight in the L0-L9 ladder. Ten addresses wrote roughly four fifths of all feedback on this registry, so a rank that counted vouches would be climbable by ten addresses.

definitions.title: Rated agents we have also watched pay
definitions.definition: Agents that both received on-chain feedback and were independently observed making a real payment.
definitions.method: The intersection of the reputation set and the L7 set. This is the overlap between what somebody says about an agent and what we watched it do.
excludes: Agents outside our tracked set.
does_not_assert: That the feedback about them is accurate. The overlap is small, which is itself the point: reputation and observed behaviour are currently almost disjoint populations.

definitions.title: Distinct addresses that have left feedback
definitions.definition: Distinct client addresses appearing as the author of a feedback event.
definitions.method: Group feedback events by their indexed author address.
excludes: Chains we do not scan.
does_not_assert: That the raters are independent. A large rater count sits alongside extreme concentration by volume, and the concentration is the more informative half.

definitions.title: Share of feedback written by the ten busiest raters
definitions.definition: Feedback events authored by the ten most prolific rater addresses, divided by all feedback events.
definitions.method: Group every event by its indexed rater address, take the ten largest, divide by the total.
does_not_assert: That prolific rating is dishonest. Bulk rating is a legitimate thing for an indexer or a scoring service to do — it just means the signal describes those services rather than a crowd.
That the ten addresses are distinct parties. One operator running ten raters would look identical from outside.

definitions.title: Share of feedback written by the single busiest rater
definitions.definition: Feedback events authored by the most prolific address, divided by all feedback events.
definitions.method: Group by author address and take the largest.
does_not_assert: That prolific rating is dishonest. Bulk rating is a legitimate thing for an indexer to do — it just means the signal describes that indexer rather than a crowd.

definitions.title: Share of feedback carrying the single most common tag
definitions.definition: Feedback events carrying the most frequent tag, divided by all feedback events.
definitions.method: Group by tag and take the largest. Grouping by author shows ten addresses wrote half the ratings; grouping by tag shows one vouching programme wrote nearly three quarters of them.
excludes: Events with no readable tag.
does_not_assert: That the tag is meaningless. It asserts that on-chain reputation is currently dominated by one programme, so treating the total as a broad social signal would misread it.

definitions.title: Total stablecoin float
definitions.definition: The aggregate circulating supply of stablecoins across all chains, as reported by DefiLlama.
definitions.method: Read from DefiLlama's stablecoins endpoint. We do not reproduce it.
excludes: Anything DefiLlama does not track.
does_not_assert: That this money is available to agents, or connected to them in any way. It is the pool the agent economy is drawn from, published as context so a reader can see how small the measured agent numbers are beside it.
That the figure is precise. Stablecoin supply is revised, and bridged representations can be double-counted by any aggregator.

definitions.title: Wallets swept every three hours
definitions.definition: Bound wallets whose outgoing USDC, USDT, EURC and DAI Transfer events are read every three hours.
definitions.method: eth_getLogs with the sender topic set to 2,000 wallets at a time, from the last swept block to the head. A wallet that moved money is queued for the per-wallet payment scan, which reads what it paid and checks the receipt.
excludes: Assets other than the four stablecoins.
does_not_assert: That a transfer is a payment. The sweep only decides who is read; the payment scan and the receipt check decide what counts.

definitions.title: Treasury share in stablecoins
definitions.definition: Stablecoins (USDC, USDT, EURC, DAI, USDbC) as a share of treasury.usd.total.v1.
definitions.method: As treasury.usd.total.v1.

definitions.title: Treasury share in DeFi positions
definitions.definition: Recognised DeFi receipts (lending supply tokens, vault shares), net of recognised debt tokens, as a share of treasury.usd.total.v1.
definitions.method: Recognised by token name and symbol against a short published list (Aave, Morpho, Moonwell, Compound, Euler, Fluid, Spark, Beefy, Yearn); anything else priced is a token.
excludes: Positions the list does not recognise, which fall into tokens.
does_not_assert: The yield earned.

definitions.title: Treasury share in ETH
definitions.definition: ETH, WETH and liquid-staking ETH tokens as a share of treasury.usd.total.v1.
definitions.method: As treasury.usd.total.v1.

definitions.title: Treasury share in other tokens
definitions.definition: Priced tokens that are not stablecoins, ETH or recognised DeFi positions, as a share of treasury.usd.total.v1.
definitions.method: As treasury.usd.total.v1.
excludes: Unpriced tokens.

definitions.title: What ranked agents hold
definitions.definition: The priced holdings of wallets bound to agents at L7 or above: stablecoins, ETH and ETH-like tokens, recognised DeFi positions net of recognised debt, and other tokens with a market price.
definitions.method: Balances from alchemy_getTokenBalances and eth_getBalance; prices from Alchemy's Prices API, refreshed daily. A wallet bound to several agents is counted once.
excludes: Tokens without a price (mostly airdropped spam): counted, never valued.
NFTs and positions held outside the wallet.
does_not_assert: That the tokens could be sold at that price.

definitions.title: Agent treasuries read
definitions.definition: Wallets bound to agents at L7 or above whose full ERC-20 and ETH holdings were read.
definitions.method: alchemy_getTokenBalances per wallet, ETH from a public node, prices from Alchemy's Prices API by token address.
does_not_assert: That the holdings belong to the agent rather than its operator.

definitions.title: DeFi TVL on Base
definitions.definition: Total value locked on Base as reported by DefiLlama.
definitions.method: Read from DefiLlama. Not reproduced.
excludes: Other chains.
does_not_assert: Any connection to agents.

definitions.title: DeFi TVL, sum of chains
definitions.definition: The sum of DefiLlama's per-chain TVL figures (its /v2/chains endpoint) at the time of reading. This is the 'TVL by chain' universe, which is smaller than the headline total on DefiLlama's home page: that headline adds categories the per-chain figures leave out (liquid staking, double-counted deposits, borrowed value) when its toggles are on. On 27 September 2026 the two read $96B and $126B for the same moment.
definitions.method: Read from DefiLlama's chains endpoint every few minutes and summed. Not reproduced.
excludes: Liquid staking, double counting and borrowed value, which the per-chain figures exclude by DefiLlama's default.
Whatever else DefiLlama's methodology excludes; theirs is the definition here, not ours.
does_not_assert: Any connection to agents. Pure market context.

definitions.title: Native USDC on Base
definitions.definition: Supply of Circle-issued native USDC on Base.
definitions.method: Read from DefiLlama's per-chain breakdown.
excludes: Bridged USDC representations, which are a different asset with a different issuer risk.
does_not_assert: That this is agent money. It is the pool on the chain we measure agents on.

definitions.title: USDC in circulation
definitions.definition: Circulating USDC supply across all chains, as reported by DefiLlama.
definitions.method: Read from DefiLlama. Not reproduced by us.
excludes: Non-USDC stablecoins.
does_not_assert: That agents hold any particular share of it.

definitions.title: USDC share of stablecoin float
definitions.definition: Circulating USDC divided by total stablecoin float.
definitions.method: Arithmetic on the two DefiLlama figures above.
does_not_assert: That agent payments split the same way. They do not — agent payment volume we observe is overwhelmingly USDC, far above USDC's share of float, and conflating the two would misstate both.

definitions.title: USDT in circulation
definitions.definition: Circulating USDT supply across all chains, as reported by DefiLlama.
definitions.method: Read from DefiLlama. Not reproduced by us.
excludes: Non-USDT stablecoins.
does_not_assert: That USDT is used by agents. In our own payment observations it barely appears; it is published so the USDC share below has a denominator a reader can check.

definitions.title: Agent-accessible vault cash
definitions.definition: Total assets held by the tracked ERC-4626 agent vault, read from the contract.
definitions.method: eth_call of totalAssets() against the vault. This one number is ours, read from the chain rather than taken from a dashboard.
excludes: Every other vault. This is one contract, not a category total.
does_not_assert: That the deposits belong to agents. A vault does not record whether its depositor is a person or a program, and we do not infer it.

definitions.title: Bound wallets delegated under EIP-7702
definitions.window: most recent code read per wallet
definitions.definition: Bound wallets whose on-chain code is exactly the EIP-7702 delegation designator 0xef0100 followed by a 20-byte implementation address.
definitions.method: eth_getCode per wallet. The designator is 23 bytes and nothing else in Ethereum produces that shape, so this is read, never inferred.
excludes: Wallets whose code we failed to read — they are not counted as undelegated, they are simply not counted.
does_not_assert: That the delegation is malicious, or that the implementation is a 'god key'. Unknown is not the same as unsafe; see the curated allowlist, which ships empty.

definitions.title: Distinct EIP-7702 implementations in use
definitions.definition: How many distinct implementation contracts the delegated wallets point at.
definitions.method: Read the implementation address out of each delegation designator and count distinct values.
excludes: Wallets that have not delegated.
does_not_assert: That each implementation is a different codebase. Two addresses can hold identical bytecode.

definitions.title: Share of examined wallets that have delegated
definitions.definition: Wallets carrying an EIP-7702 delegation designator, divided by wallets whose code we read.
definitions.method: A delegated account's code is exactly 23 bytes: the 0xef0100 prefix followed by the implementation address. Anything else is not a delegation.
excludes: Wallets whose code we failed to read.
does_not_assert: That delegation is dangerous. It is how a wallet gets batching, sponsorship and session keys.
That the wallet's owner understands what the implementation does. That is the actual risk, and it is not measurable from the designator.

definitions.title: Share of delegated wallets on the four busiest implementations
definitions.definition: Delegated wallets pointing at any of the four most-used implementations, divided by all delegated wallets.
definitions.method: As above, taking the top four.
excludes: Undelegated wallets.
does_not_assert: That these four are related, or audited, or unaudited. We publish the concentration, not a judgement of the code.

definitions.title: Share of delegated wallets on the single busiest implementation
definitions.definition: Delegated wallets pointing at the most-used implementation, divided by all delegated wallets.
definitions.method: Group delegated wallets by implementation address and take the largest.
excludes: Undelegated wallets.
does_not_assert: That the leading implementation is unsafe. It asserts concentration: a bug in one contract would reach this share of delegated agent wallets at once, which is a systemic fact worth knowing regardless of that contract's quality.

definitions.title: Wallets whose code we have read
definitions.definition: Bound wallets for which we have successfully read the account's code.
definitions.method: eth_getCode per wallet. A failed read is recorded as a failure and the wallet is excluded from both numerator and denominator of the delegation rate — never silently assumed undelegated.
excludes: Wallets whose code we could not read.
does_not_assert: That code is static. Delegation can be set and revoked, which is why delegated wallets are re-read daily and undelegated ones weekly.

definitions.title: x402 payers that are ERC-8004 agents
definitions.definition: Distinct addresses that paid an x402 Bazaar seller on Base in the last seven days, how many of them are wallets bound to an ERC-8004 identity on Base, and the share of the dollars those bound wallets paid.
definitions.method: Stablecoin transfers into the payTo addresses of Bazaar sellers, read from the chain (x402.seller.*), joined to open bindings.
excludes: Sellers not listed in the Bazaar.
Other chains, where we do not bind identities.
does_not_assert: That an unbound payer is not an agent: most x402 buyers never registered an identity.

definitions.title: Our observed payments on the x402 rail
definitions.definition: Payments we watched leave a bound agent wallet and land on a known x402 recipient address.
definitions.method: Match our own observed payments against the harvested recipient set. Measured on our data, not taken from anyone's dashboard.
excludes: Payments to x402 recipients we do not know about.
does_not_assert: That the payment used the x402 protocol. Landing on a known x402 recipient is strong evidence of the rail, not proof of the handshake.

definitions.title: Share of observed agent payments on the x402 rail
definitions.definition: Of the payments we have observed leaving bound agent wallets, the share that landed on an address publicly indexed as an x402 payment recipient.
definitions.method: Recipient addresses are harvested from a public x402 resource index and stored with the source URL against each address. An observed transfer whose destination is in that set is marked rail=x402.
excludes: Payments on any chain but Base.
Recipients we cannot cite — the address set never grows by guesswork.
does_not_assert: That this is the true x402 share. It is a FLOOR: the recipient set comes from one public catalogue, walked in rotation at about a day per full pass, and any x402 recipient that catalogue does not list, or that the walk has not reached yet, makes this number smaller than reality. Until 2026-09-18 the harvest re-read only the first 2,000 of roughly 51,000 listings, so earlier values undercount more heavily and the step up on that date is coverage, not growth.
That a payment to an indexed recipient used the x402 protocol. The address is strong evidence of the rail, not proof of the handshake.
definitions.source: AFG-Pulse rail attribution over x402scan's published recipients

definitions.title: USD value of our observed x402 payments
definitions.definition: The summed value of those payments.
definitions.method: As above, summing recorded USD value.
excludes: The same exclusions as the event count.
does_not_assert: That x402 volume is negligible in general. It says the attributed value we can see is tiny — these are micro-payments, and the whole attributed set is worth less than a dollar.

definitions.title: Unique x402 payers in 24 hours
definitions.definition: Distinct paying addresses reported by x402scan for the last day.
definitions.method: Read from x402scan. Not reproduced.
does_not_assert: That a payer is an agent, or that one address is one party.

definitions.title: Known x402 recipient addresses
definitions.definition: How many x402 payment-recipient addresses we hold, harvested from a cited public index.
definitions.method: Harvested with the source URL stored against every member, and published in full as an address set. No address enters by assertion.
excludes: Recipients the public index does not list, which is most of them.
does_not_assert: That this is the x402 recipient population. It is a floor, and every recipient it misses makes our attributed share smaller than reality.

definitions.title: Share of indexed x402 resources that answer
definitions.definition: Of the indexed resources we probed, the share that returned a payment challenge or a valid response rather than nothing.
definitions.method: Our own probe against a sample of the catalogue. This one is measured by us, not cited.
excludes: Resources we did not probe.
does_not_assert: That a live resource has ever been paid. Answering a request is a much weaker claim than trading.

definitions.title: x402 resources indexed
definitions.definition: Total x402 resources listed by the cited index.
definitions.method: Read from x402scan. Not reproduced.
excludes: Resources the index does not list.
does_not_assert: That the resources are live. It is a catalogue size, and the share that actually answers a request is published beside it.

definitions.title: Registered agents paying Bazaar sellers, 24 hours
definitions.definition: Of the wallets in x402.seller.payers.24h.v1, those with an open binding to an ERC-8004 registration.
definitions.method: Payers joined to open bindings.
does_not_assert: That unbound payers are not agents. Most software that pays for APIs has not registered an identity; this measures the overlap, not the population.

definitions.title: Transfers into Bazaar sellers, 24 hours
definitions.definition: Count of the transfers in x402.seller.inflow.usd.24h.v1.
definitions.method: As x402.seller.inflow.usd.24h.v1.
does_not_assert: That each transfer is one API call.

definitions.title: USDC into Bazaar sellers, 24 hours
definitions.definition: USDC transferred in the last 24 hours to the payTo addresses that sellers declare in Coinbase's x402 Bazaar on Base.
definitions.method: eth_getLogs for USDC Transfer events with the recipient topic set to the listed payTo addresses, every three hours from a cursor; the seller list is re-read from the Bazaar every six hours.
excludes: Mints to a seller address.
Sellers not listed in the Bazaar.
does_not_assert: That every inflow was an x402 settlement: a payTo address can receive other transfers, so this is an upper bound for listed sellers and a floor for x402 overall.

definitions.title: Wallets paying Bazaar sellers, 24 hours
definitions.definition: Distinct senders of the transfers in x402.seller.inflow.usd.24h.v1.
definitions.method: As x402.seller.inflow.usd.24h.v1.
does_not_assert: That a wallet is an agent, or that different wallets are different operators.

definitions.title: Bazaar sellers receiving, 24 hours
definitions.definition: Listed payTo addresses that received at least one USDC transfer in the last 24 hours.
definitions.method: As x402.seller.inflow.usd.24h.v1.
does_not_assert: That one address is one company.

definitions.title: Active x402 servers
definitions.definition: Servers reported active by x402scan.
definitions.method: Read from x402scan. Not reproduced.
does_not_assert: That an active server has customers. Our own probe of listed resources finds a substantial share do not answer.

definitions.title: Transfers into Bazaar sellers on Solana, 24 hours
definitions.definition: Successful transactions that increased the USDC token account of a seller listed in the Bazaar on Solana.
definitions.method: The seller's USDC token account from getTokenAccountsByOwner; its signatures from getSignaturesForAddress; each new transaction read once with getTransaction and counted when the account's USDC balance went up.
excludes: Failed transactions.
Transactions that moved USDC out of the account.
does_not_assert: That every inflow was an x402 settlement.

definitions.title: USDC into Bazaar sellers on Solana, 24 hours
definitions.definition: USD value of the transfers in x402.solana.settlements.24h.v1.
definitions.method: As x402.solana.settlements.24h.v1.
does_not_assert: That every inflow was an x402 settlement.

definitions.title: Disagreement between public x402 counters
definitions.chain_set: eip155:8453 (Base) for one source; the other does not state its chain set
definitions.definition: The larger public x402 transaction count divided by the smaller, across two independent third-party indexes.
definitions.method: agenteconomy.to's daily x402 figure against x402scan's 24-hour Base figure.
does_not_assert: That either counter is wrong. Neither is auditable from outside, and they may simply count different things — which is the point of publishing the ratio instead of a winner.
That the windows are identical. One is a calendar day, the other a rolling 24 hours, and that alone cannot explain a gap of this size.

definitions.title: Share of x402 traffic on testnet
definitions.definition: Transactions on Base Sepolia divided by transactions on Base Sepolia plus Base mainnet, per x402scan.
definitions.method: Directly from the publisher's per-chain breakdown, which flags each chain as mainnet or not.
excludes: Chains the publisher does not report.
does_not_assert: That testnet activity is worthless. It asserts that a headline combining the two is not measuring money.

definitions.title: x402 transactions in 24 hours, per x402scan
definitions.definition: Transactions reported by x402scan for the last day.
definitions.method: Read from x402scan. Not reproduced.
does_not_assert: That these are mainnet, or human-free. A share of indexed activity is testnet, and that share is published separately so this number is read with it.

definitions.title: x402 transactions, cumulative (cited)
definitions.definition: Total x402 transactions as reported by the cited index.
definitions.method: Read from the source. Not reproduced.
excludes: Whatever the index does not cover.
does_not_assert: That these were agent payments. The rail does not distinguish a program from a person, and neither does the counter.
That it agrees with the other x402 counter we publish. The two differ by roughly an order of magnitude.

definitions.title: x402 24-hour volume, normalised
definitions.definition: The same 24-hour volume after correcting for token decimal handling in the source feed.
definitions.method: Applied by us to the cited figure. Published alongside the raw number rather than replacing it, so the correction is visible instead of silent.
does_not_assert: That our normalisation is authoritative. It is our reading of their feed, and the ratio between the two is published so a reader can judge it.

definitions.title: x402 volume in 24 hours, per x402scan
definitions.definition: Payment volume reported by x402scan for the last day, as published.
definitions.method: Read from x402scan. Not reproduced.
does_not_assert: That the figure is denominated the way you expect. A normalised version and the ratio between them are published beside it, because the raw number and the normalised one differ enough to change the story.

definitions.title: Ratio between raw and normalised x402 volume
definitions.definition: The normalised 24-hour volume divided by the raw published figure.
definitions.method: Arithmetic. Its only job is to make the size of the correction impossible to miss.
does_not_assert: That either figure is correct. It measures the distance between them.

definitions.title: x402 volume, cumulative (cited)
definitions.definition: Total x402 payment volume as reported by the cited index.
definitions.method: Read from the source. Not reproduced.
excludes: Whatever the index does not cover.
does_not_assert: That the volume is agent volume, or that it is denominated consistently across the index.

definitions.title: Stablecoins sent by owners on other chains, 30 days
definitions.definition: USD value of the transfers counted in xchain.owners.paying.30d.v1.
definitions.method: As xchain.owners.paying.30d.v1.
excludes: As xchain.owners.paying.30d.v1.
does_not_assert: Agent spending. See xchain.owners.paying.30d.v1.

definitions.title: Owner wallets on other chains
definitions.definition: Distinct (chain, owner) pairs over xchain.registrations.v1.
definitions.method: As xchain.registrations.v1.
excludes: Burn and zero addresses.
does_not_assert: Who operates the wallet.

definitions.title: Owners sending stablecoins on other chains, 30 days
definitions.definition: Owner wallets from xchain.owner.wallets.v1 that sent USDC, bridged USDC or USDT to another address in the last 30 days, at or after the block of their first registration on that chain.
definitions.method: eth_getLogs with the sender topic set to 1,000 owners at a time, per chain, from a cursor.
excludes: Transfers before the owner's first registration on that chain.
Self-transfers.
does_not_assert: That a transfer is a purchase: these are not yet receipt-checked for routing hops the way Base payments are, so they are published as transfers, not as agent spending.

definitions.title: ERC-8004 registrations on other chains
definitions.definition: Registrations in the ERC-8004 Identity registry at the same address on Ethereum, Arbitrum One, OP Mainnet and Polygon PoS, with a current owner.
definitions.method: Alchemy NFT API getOwnersForContract per chain, daily.
excludes: Base, which is counted separately and never added to this.
does_not_assert: That a registration is an operating agent.
